articleTitle: Research on compact Q-band 5G RF array
abstract: A compact Q band wave RF array for 5G millimeter communication system is reported in this presentation. The array has 16 RF channels and 256 antenna cells. The transmitter and receiver are designed using multi-layered configuration to decrease the module size. The antenna array and feeding structure are designed and integrated in RF module. The size of fabricated RF array is 20cm∗20cm. IF and power supply circuits are also designed separately to support the RF array. Performance of transmitter and receiver array are measured which could be applied in Q-band millimeter wave massive MIMO system.

articleTitle: Placement selection of millimeter wave FMCW radar for indoor fall detection
abstract: Indoor fall detection based on radar technology has recently drawn more and more attention because of the advantages of privacy protection, all-day working and non-intrusive properties. Numerous studies have used Micro-Doppler information to extract fall signatures. However, mounting position of a radar sensor has a great influence on the Doppler response and fall signature extraction. In this work, we demonstrate the effects of radar placements on micro-Doppler and range intensity. For this purpose, we first use an approximation rigid-motion model to analyze the process of a fall. Then time-frequency distribution and range-time intensity are used as the input data for feature extraction. A millimeter wave frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar with 3-GHz bandwidth is mounted on three positions to detect the action of human fall. Experimental results show that well selected placement of the radar sensor can provide improved feature extraction results both from micro-Doppler and range-time intensity.

articleTitle: Multi-coil high efficiency wireless power transfer system against misalignment
abstract: The power transfer efficiency of magnetic-resonance coupled wireless power transfer (WPT) systems is sensitive to the alignment of coils. In this paper, a novel multi-coil WPT system is proposed to enhance power transfer efficiency. It can overcome the misalignment problem and maintain high power transfer efficiency. The proposed coil loop structure can provide a strong magnetic resonance coupling between the Tx and Rx coils. There are four induvial resonators applied in the system and it demonstrates that at least a pair of coupled resonators in several misaligned conditions could realize high power transfer efficiency over a misaligned distance. The experimental results show that the proposed multi-loop WPT system can achieve 90.2% peak efficiency when the coils are well aligned. Mean-while, this WPT system maintains over 70% efficiency over a misalignment distance from 0 to 55 mm, which is about 66% of the length of the Rx board. The proposed WPT system could be used either in implant devices for biomedical healthcare and treatment or for electric vehicles charging systems.

articleTitle: A 24–30 GHz CMOS LNA with 2.05dB NF and 0.6dB in-band gain ripple for 5G-applications
abstract: This paper presents a low noise amplifier (LNA) for 28 GHz communication system of 5G-applications. The proposed LNA composes of three differential amplifier stages. A common-gate stage acts as the first one for broadband input impedance matching and two cascode stages followed for a higher gain. In order to reduce the noise and improve the gain, the gm-boost technique based on capacitor cross-coupled is employed. Besides, parallel-LC matching network is applied at the output to reduce the return loss. Furthermore, the peak gain of each stage is separated and tuned respectively for a flat gain. This LNA is designed and simulated utilizing 65 nm CMOS process. The post-layout simulation shows that a gain of 30.5 dB with ±0.3 dB gain ripple in 24–30 GHz and a minimum noise figure (NF) of 2.05 dB at 25.5 GHz are achieved. The proposed differential LNA dissipates 30 mW with a 1 V power supply.

articleTitle: Dual-input driving strategies for performance enhancement of a doherty power amplifier
abstract: The aim of this work is to assess the performance improvement offered by several driving strategies of a dual-input digital Doherty power amplifier with respect to the equivalent single-input topology. To offer a fair comparison, an analog amplifier and the equivalent digital version, which is equal in all parts except for the absence of the input power divider, are designed at 3.5 GHz. The flexibility of a dual-input control allows to implement power-dependent input signal splitting and phase alignment between the main and auxiliary branches, thus allowing to overcome several shortcomings of traditional analog Doherty amplifiers. The proposed analysis focuses on the gain and efficiency performance over a 6 dB back-off range. The comparison over the 3.1-3.7 GHz range shows a superior performance of the digital DPA over the analog one, thus justifying the additional.

articleTitle: Compact resonators in substrate integrated waveguide technology
abstract: The substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology can be used to develop high-quality microwave components, but the resulting devices are relatively large compared to other planar technologies. The half-mode SIW and quarter-mode SIW topologies offer reduction in space, but they are open resonator and lead to additional losses. To provide a guideline in the choice of the appropriate technology in the filter design, a systematic study of the characteristic of compact SIW resonators is presented. Moreover, a solution to improve the performance of these open resonators using partial electromagnetic shielding is introduced. A filter based on shielded quarter-mode SIW resonators is reported and experimentally validated.

articleTitle: Range-gating technology for millimeter-wave radar remote gesture control in IoT applications
abstract: Touchless hand gesture using portable millimeter-wave radar sensors an enabling technology for Internet of Things (IoT) applications. In this paper, we investigate the feasibility of using a frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar with noise removal and range gating method to recognize human hand gesture for a user moving in the radar's field of view. These detected hand gestures will be applied to remote control of computers or smart TVs at a distance from 0.3 m to 1.2 m.

articleTitle: A 26 GHz Doherty power amplifier and a fully integrated 2×2 PA in 0.15μm GaN HEMT process for heterogeneous integration and 5G
abstract: A 26 GHz Doherty power amplifier MMIC and a fully integrated 2×2 PA array based on the DPA are presented in this paper. The Doherty power amplifier using 0.15μm GaN HEMT technology, achieves maximum small signal gain of 13.6 dB and saturated output power of over 32 dBm in 24-28 GHz, with peak PAE of 21.7%, and 6 dB back-off PAE of 20% at 26 GHz. The 2×2 power MMIC consists of 4 symmetric proposed Doherty PAs with signal interconnections on the backside and specialized optimizations of layouts for 3D heterogeneous integration technology, which is suitable for 5G Massive MIMO applications. The chip size of single Doherty power amplifier and monolithic power amplifier array are 2.5 × 2.0 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 5.0 × 5.0 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> respectively.

articleTitle: A 60 GHz low noise variable gain amplifier with small noise figure and IIP3 variation in a 40-nm CMOS technology
abstract: This paper presents the design and measurement of a low noise variable gain amplifier (VGA) over the frequency band of 57 GHz and 64 GHz, using 40-nm CMOS technology. The design applies an inductive degeneration technique for simultaneously noise and power matching, a layout gate inductance for gain frequency extension, and current steering technique for gain tuning. The comparison of a low noise amplifier (LNA) and a low noise VGA is done, in terms of noise figure and linearity (IIP3). The LNA achieves 6.7 dB gain and 4.3 dB noise figure (NF) at 60 GHz, while consuming 12 mA from a 1.1 V supply. The IIP3 of the LNA is -12.8 dBm. The VGA has an S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> of 6.67 dB (maximum) and 5.1 dB NF at 58 GHz. The gain tuning range is 6 dB and the NF deviation is 0.8 dB at 60 GHz and the IIP3 is -7.66 dBm at the maximum gain state. The supply voltage of the VGA is 1.1 V and the DC current is 11 mA.

articleTitle: Capacity evaluation on the long-distance orbital angular momentum non-orthogonal transmission
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) wave with Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) can achieve high channel capacity via OAM mode multiplexing. However, due to the beam divergence angle, it is impossible to receive the whole phase front in long-distance. Consequently, partial aperture receiving gradually draws attention in the long-distance OAM transmission. In this paper, the channel capacity of such long-distance non-orthogonal transmission is analyzed. Specifically, the long-distance OAM non-orthogonal transmission system structure and the mathematical model of the channel capacity are established. Meanwhile, simulations are carried out to evaluate the channel capacities. Compared with the plane wave received by antenna array, the OAM non-orthogonal transmission can also result in a significant channel capacity gain. Similar to the Multiple-Input and Multiple-Output (MIMO) system, the capacity gain non-linearly decreases when the multiplexed OAM modes increase, which means a limited number of OAM modes is sufficient and appreciated in the practical applications.

articleTitle: A high-efficiency radio frequency rectifier-booster regulator for ambient WLAN energy harvesting applications
abstract: In this paper, a novel high-efficiency rectifier-booster regulator operating in radio frequency (RF) is firstly proposed. Then an entire WLAN energy harvesting system is demonstrated. A flower-shaped broadband dual-polarized cross dipole rectenna with matching network is employed to harvest electromagnetic energy from a WiFi router. A novel rectifier-booster regulator (RBR) is proposed to rectify the AC energy to DC and boost the high output voltage. It evolves from a Grein-acher rectifier and two Dickson charge pump to form a full wave rectifier. The measurement results show that the RBR can achieve up to ×3.4 voltage boosting with 85% voltage conversion efficiency (VCE) and provide over 1 V output voltage within a distance of 50 cm between a power amplifier (PA) with 20 dBm transmitting power and the rectenna. Maximum energy of 245 μW is harvested by the entire system. The good performance shows its wide practicality for Internet-of-Thing (IoT) applications.

articleTitle: A robust and broadband digital predistortion utilizing negative feedback iteration
abstract: In this paper, a robust and broadband digital predistortion (DPD) based on negative feedback iteration technique is proposed for linearization of power amplifier with strong memory effects. Instead of estimating the DPD parameters directly in conventional direct learning architecture, the proposed DPD identifies the optimal DPD signal which eliminates the modeling error at first and then calculate the corresponding DPD parameters. The proposed DPD can realize superior linear performance for broadband signal than conventional direct learning DPD while having a relative low computational complexity. A 2-carrier 200MHz bandwidth LTE signal at 2.1GHz DPD test is carried out for validation, which achieves better than 11.8dB ACPR correction and outperforms conventional direct leaning method.

articleTitle: Nonlinearity correction for range estimation in FMCW millimeter-wave automotive radar
abstract: In this paper, we propose a computational correction algorithm to reduce the effect of source nonlinearity on range estimation for millimeter-wave frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) automotive radars. With a transient parametric modeling on the source nonlinearity function, the proposed algorithm aims to jointly estimate range parameters from multiple reflectors and parametric nonlinearity coefficients from the beat signal, without using a reference (either a dedicated delay line or a reflector at a known distance). Numerical results are provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband metamaterial absorber using three-layer ring and patch resonators
abstract: This paper proposes a three-layer ultra-wideband metamaterial absorber, which consists of layered ring resonators and four rectangular patch resonators on the top. The structure is rotationally symmetrical and hence becomes polarization-insensitive. This absorber realizes an absorption bandwidth of 22.39 GHz within 6.37–28.76 GHz for absorptivity level above 90%. The overall thickness of this absorber is 4.9mm, which is only 0.10X and 0.21X at the lowest and highest frequencies, respectively. The proposed structure exhibits wider absorption bandwidth in comparison with the state of arts.

articleTitle: Design of the quarter-mode substrate integrated waveguide in-phase and out-of-phase filtering power divider
abstract: In this paper, a series of the quarter-mode substrate integrated waveguide (QMSIW) Altering power dividers (FPD)s with compact size are proposed. The FPDs are designed in two forms which are in-phase and out-of-phase topologies, respectively. As for the in-phase FPD, two QMSIW cavities are coupled by the inductive windows in the single-layered substrate to obtain a two-pole filtering response. As for the out-of-phase FPD, the multilayer substrate integrated waveguide structure is utilized to achieve a 180° reverse phase characteristic between two outputs. Measured results show that, the proposed in-phase QMSIW FPD has a 3-dB fractional bandwidth of 41.4% (4.6-7 GHz). Moreover, the amplitude and phase imbalances are measured less than 0.3 dB and 2.4°, respectively. The out-of-phase QMSIW FPD is measured at 5.8 GHz. In addition, the amplitude and phase imbalances are measured less than 1 dB and 2.6°, individually.

articleTitle: A K-band power amplifier in a 0.15-um GaAs pHEMT process
abstract: A K-band monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) power amplifier (PA) is designed using a 0.15 um Emode GaAs pHEMT process. The MMIC PA is designed with power combining technology. Simulation results show that the MMIC PA exhibits saturation output power (Psat) of 31 dBm with power added efficiency (PAE) higher than 27.3%, and power gain higher than 21.3 dB from 24 GHz to 28 GHz, the input return loss is lower than -13dB, and the output return loss is lower than -12dB in the working band. Furthermore, the chip size is 3mm*1.5mm including all the bonding pads.

articleTitle: A reconfigurable multi-ratio charge pump with wide input/output voltage range for wireless energy harvesting system
abstract: A charge pump (CP) with reconfigurable multi-ratio is proposed for wireless energy harvesting system, which has almost eight ratios with small step to suit for wide input or output voltage range applications. Six flying capacitors are adopted to generate different conversion ratios (CRs) from ×0.25 to ×2 with step of 0.25. The CR of the CP is determined by input voltage and on-chip control unit. Thus, an almost constant output voltage is obtained in a wide input voltage range. Besides, the MOS switches of the CP are driven by a two-phase non-overlapping clock to reduce quiescent current and improve the power conversion efficiency (PCE). As a result, a configurable CP is achieved by using a standard 0.35 μm CMOS process with 1.7 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> die area (include PADs.) The output voltage of the CP can be kept almost constant at 3.6 V when Vin varies from 1.77 V to 4.80 V. The PCE is over 80% no matter which CR is, and the maximum PCE of 93.8% is achieved when Vin=3.6 and CR=1 @ 1.2 KΩ load resistance. The wide input/output voltage range and PCE of the proposed CP shows its good practicality for DC-DC converter of wireless energy harvesting system.

articleTitle: Constant capacitive wireless power transfer at variable coupling
abstract: Capacitive wireless power transfer uses the varying electric field for wireless power transfer from a transmitter plate to a receiver plate. The amount of power transferred to the load and the system efficiency are dependent of the coupling between transmitter and receiver. However, by changing the operating frequency, it is possible to achieve constant power transfer and efficiency, even at variable coupling. In this work, the analytical expressions for the three different gains of a general capacitive wireless power transfer system are calculated. Based on the gains, an analytical solution is determined for achieving constant power transfer and efficiency at variable coupling. The analytical results are validated by circuital simulation in SPICE.

articleTitle: An efficient and extended range tracking method using a hybrid FSK-FMCW system
abstract: Radar systems are considered suitable sensors for detection of moving objects and motion-based tracking. Among various radar types, frequency-shift keying (FSK) radar are attractive for being able to track the absolute range of a moving target with little bandwidth requirement and free from surrounding background clutter interference. However, its maximum unambiguous range is limited due to the periodicity of the phase difference over 2n and it is inversely proportional to the frequency shift between two transmitted frequencies, while its measurement resolution is proportional to this frequency shift. Frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar has no range limitation on target tracking but occupies a large bandwidth. Therefore, in this paper, a hybrid FSK-FMCW system is proposed by using a short-time operating FMCW system with small bandwidth as reference to increase the FSK system maximum discernable range without losing measurement resolution. Range tracking experiment of a human subject was conducted and results are presented to demonstrate the performance of the proposed hybrid method.

articleTitle: A low-profile dual-polarized stacked patch antenna for micro-base-station applications
abstract: This paper presents a low-profile dual-polarized stacked patch antenna for micro-base-station applications. The proposed antenna includes three antenna elements, where each element consists of two rectangular patches, substrate and reflector. By introducing dual-feed technique, dual-polarization characteristic is achieved. The bandwidth is improved by couple patch. Measured results show that the proposed antenna can operate in 1710 to 1980 MHz (impedance bandwidth of 14.6%) with S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub><;-15 dB, and has stable radiation pattern with halfpower beamwidth (HPBW) of 65° ±5° at H plane and stability gain of 12 dBi. In addition, the total height of the antenna is only 0.083A. The proposed antenna with the compact structure, low-profile and stable gain is very suitable for micro-base-station applications.

articleTitle: A Ka-band 65-nm CMOS neutralized medium power amplifier for 5G phased-array applications
abstract: This paper presents a Ka-band neutralized medium power amplifier (PA). The two-stage single-path PA adopts the neutralizing capacitors to increase the stability and three types of transformers to simplify the design of impedance matching networks. The push-pull common-source configuration is employed in each stage to enhance the efficiency. Designed and implemented in 65nm CMOS technology with 1-V supply, the prototype delivers a saturated output power (P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</sub>) of 13 dBm from 27-33 GHz with the maximum small-signal gain of 18 dB. The measured maximum P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</sub> is 13.77 dBm at 30 GHz with corresponding 1dB compression power (P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</sub>) of 12.67 dBm and power-added efficiency (PAE) of 29.8%. The chip size is only 0.18 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> excluding all DC pads.

articleTitle: A compact millimeter wave (mmWave) mid-field over the air (OTA) RF performance test system for 5G massive MIMO devices
abstract: A 5G mmWave Massive MIMO device needs to perform the phase coherency calibration and RF parametric measurement over the air (OTA). The device size and the array size make it very challenging to do RF parametric measurement in the true far field OTA environment from the space, link budget and cost aspects. To meet the requirement on very compact size, a mmWave mid-field OTA RF performance test system is designed in this paper. This system can do the phase coherency calibration and support the RF parametric measurements per the 3GPP requirements. An overview of the system design challenges and measurement approaches is provided together with the experiment validation of the functionalities of the system to prove the effectiveness of the system for 5G massive MIMO device OTA RF calibration and parametric measurement.

articleTitle: Overview of 5G UE OTA performance test challenges and methods
abstract: This paper analyzes the challenges for 5G OTA performance test and contrasts the advantages and limitations of the methods being considered in 3GPP for mmWave UE demodulation test. It first introduces the concepts and setups of MPAC and RTS test methods, which are widely studied for 4G UE MIMO OTA test, then analyzes potential issues when extending these methods to 5G demodulation tests and proposes possible solutions to the open issues. Currently, different test methods, including IF testing, SS-MPAC method with direct spatial channel emulation and applying RTS method with baseband emulation of Multi-AoA, are all under discussion in 3GPP for mmWave UE demodulation testing. This paper contrasts the limitations and advantages of different methods.

articleTitle: Support vector regression-based dynamic behavioral modeling for RF power amplifiers
abstract: A new dynamic behavioral modelling technique, based on support vector regression (SVR), is presented in this paper. As an advanced machine learning technique, the SVR method provides an effective option for behavioral modeling of radio frequency (RF) power amplifiers (PAs) including the nonlinear and memory effects. In this paper, the basic theory of the proposed SVR modelling method is provided, along with details on model implementation of RF PAs. Experimental test example for a LDMOS PA is presented, revealing that the new modelling methodology provides a very efficient and extremely accurate prediction.

articleTitle: Novel Gysel power dividers based on Half-Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide (HMSIW)
abstract: This paper presents novel Gysel power dividers by combining Half-Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide(HMSIW) power dividers and microstrip-based isolation networks, which achieve the isolations between two distributing ports and high power-handling capability. The proposed Gysel power divider has SIW sections, two HMSIW sections, microstrip network and adaptors between SIW/HMSIW to microstrip for measurement with coaxial connectors. The proposed concept is investigated and analyzed by using even-odd method. For demonstration, a prototype is designed, fabricated and measured. Good performances were observed experimentally, showing the advantages of proposed concept and an excellent candidate for high power-handling HMSIW/SIW circuits or systems.

articleTitle: Design of broadband multi-layer metamaterial absorber
abstract: In this paper, a compact broadband metamaterial absorber is proposed. The unit cell of the proposed structure comprises two metallic layers with hexagonal patch printed over dielectric substrate. To enhance the resonate effect, the unit cell structure consists of three dielectric layers and two air layers. The simulated results of this structure show 90% absorption bandwidth of 14.2 GHz from 4.3 GHz to 19.1 GHz. To achieve this broadband, two air layers inserted to this structure to enhance the resonance effect. In this broadband, the performance of the absorber has been investigated under different oblique angles and polarization angles of the incident wave and the influence of the air layer. While the configuration is simple and with a thickness of 0.107). and a unit cell size of 0.136). (corresponding to the lowest frequency). The designed absorber is compact, thin and has potential to be used for multiple EM applications.

articleTitle: Multilayer SIW dual-mode bandpass filter with higher-order mode attenuation
abstract: In this work, we provide a multilayer structure substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) bandpass filter for Ku-band. For the multilayer structure, two substrates are stacked using low-cost and reliable PCB fabrication process and each substrate possesses a circular shaped dual-mode resonator for fourth-order response. By adopting tilted port configuration rather than typical orthogonal one, higher-order modes can be attenuated and the wider stopband characteristic is achieved. Simulation and measurement results are well matched each other.

articleTitle: Four-pole frequency agile bandpass filter with fully canonical response and constant ABW
abstract: This paper reports on the first four-order frequency-agile bandpass filter (FA-BPF) with four transmission zeros (TZs) and constant absolute bandwidth. The proposed filter employs four varactor-loaded resonators and can be controlled by only two bias. Therefore, very simple design and control procedures are achieved while the good insertion loss (IL) performance are obtained when comparing to other cross-coupling high-order tunable filter. The design starts with the element-variable coupling matrix. By synchronously tuning the element-variable coupling matrix, the center frequency (CF) of the resultant passband is tuned and the bandpass bandwidth is kept unchanged. According to the matrix, the 1.24-1.72 GHz FA-BPF with a constant ABW of 61.5±1.5 MHz is realized and measured. The measurement results validate the prediction.

articleTitle: A wideband dual-polarized magneto-electric dipole antenna for 2G/3G/LTE/WiMAX base stations
abstract: A wideband dual-polarized magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna is proposed for 2G/3G/LTE/WiMAX applications. It also applies to 5G (3.3–3.6 GHz). The proposed antenna has Γ-shaped feeding strips to impart a wide impedance bandwidth for it special structure, and a rectangular box-shaped reflector to enhance its stability in radiation patterns and high gain over the operating frequencies. The simulated results show a common impedance bandwidth is 81.2% with standing-wave ratio (SWR) ≤ 1.5 from 1.58 to 3.74 GHz, port-to-port isolation is large than 25dB within the bandwidth. The simulated antenna gains vary from 8 to 10.7 dBi and from 8.2 to 10.6 dBi for port 1 and port 2, respectively. The antenna has nearly symmetrical radiation patterns with low back lobe radiation both in horizontal and vertical planes, and broadside radiation patterns with narrow beam can be also obtained.

articleTitle: Orbital angular momentum multiplexing with non-degenerate modes in secondary frequency domain
abstract: The Electro-Magnetic (EM) waves with Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) can achieve high spectral efficiency through multiplexing of different OAM modes. Due to the divergence of the beam angle, only partial phase plane of OAM wave can be received in the long distance transmission. Recently, it is reported that the mapping of different OAM modes to the corresponding frequency shifts in the second frequency domain can be established, so that to efficiently identify the OAM modes with partial phase plane reception. However, not all combinations of arbitrary OAM modes support the one-to-one mapping with frequency shifts in the second frequency domain. In other words, there is degeneracy in the combinations of different OAM modes for multiplexing transmission. Naturally, which combinations of OAM modes can be chosen to avoid the occurrence of the degeneracy in the second frequency domain becomes a fundamental problem. In this paper, the non-degenerate mode of OAM multiplexing is mathematically analyzed and evaluated. Specifically, all the non-degenerate patterns corresponding to the multiplexing combinations are enumerated with OAM numbers less than 7. Moreover, an experiment with 2 OAM modes multiplexing is carried out to illustrate the degeneracy of the OAM mode combination in the second frequency domain.

articleTitle: Integrated active quasi-circulator with 27 dB isolation and 0.8–6.8GHz wideband by using feedback technique
abstract: Circulators are widely adopted to decouple the incident and reflected waves. Active circulators have the properties such as small size, low cost and compatibility with Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) technology. With the advent of big data, circuits must have wideband characteristics to handle a large number of signals. In this paper, a new topology is proposed to realize an active quasi-circulator. Feedback technology is presented to enhance the isolation from transmitter to receiver (|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</sub>|) for wideband utilizations. The proposed circulator is fabricated with a standard 0.18 μm CMOS process. The measured bandwidth is from 0.8 GHz to 6.8 GHz, which to our knowledge is the widest ever reported in integrated circulators. The measured |S31| is higher than 27 dB. The isolations of receiver-to-transmitter (|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sub>|)receiver-to-antenna (|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">23</sub>|), and antenna-to-transmitter (|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub>|) are better than 15dB, 28 dB and 20 dB, respectively. Power consumption of the core circuit of the circulator is 12.8 mW and the chip size is 0.54 mm × 0.66 mm including bonding pads. The designed active quasi-circulator possesses high isolation and wideband simultaneously.

articleTitle: Support vector machine for channel prediction in high-speed railway communication systems
abstract: In this paper, the problem of fast time-varying channel prediction is investigated in high-speed railway communication systems. A channel prediction algorithm is proposed based on a support vector machine (SVM) model. In order to further improve the prediction accuracy, the penalty coefficient and Gaussian kernel width of the SVM model are optimized by a genetic algorithm (GA). Simulation results show that the proposed prediction model based on both the SVM and the GA (SVM-GA) has lower prediction error than traditional auto-regressive (AR) and single SVM prediction models. In addition, when the effect of the noise on prediction performance is considered, the SVM-GA prediction model is superior to the AR and the SVM models in terms of normalized mean squared error.

articleTitle: Dual-channel filter based on dielectric resonator for 5G massive MIMO system
abstract: In this paper, we present a method for designing dual-channel bandpass filters (BPFs) using dielectric resonator (DR). Two BPFs are integrated as one dual-channel filter with two input ports and two output ports. By using a common quad-mode DR shared by two second-order BPFs, only one metallic cavity is needed, which greatly reduces the circuit size. By properly arranging the input and output feeding probes, two of the resonant modes are excited for one channel and other two for the other channel. Since the feeding probes of one channel filter do not excite the resonant modes of the other one, isolation between two filters is achieved. Three transmission zeros are generated near the passband, resulting in high selectivity and good out-of-band rejection. For verification, the dual-channel filter is implemented, which features good bandpass responses and offers a significant size reduction in comparison with conventional two DR filters.

articleTitle: Beamforming UWB-IR transmitter for NLOS indoor positioning and tracking application
abstract: This paper describes a UWB-IR beamforming transmitter array for non-line-of-sight directional indoor positioning and tracking of moving objects in the dense cluttered environment. The proposed electronically controlled UWB-IR beamforming circuit uses the combination of tunable digital true-time delay cell to generate the four equally time-spaced data pulses. The equally time-spaced data pulses fed to the UWB-IR pulse generator array of four elements, which generate four UWB-IR pulses with the same amount of relative delays. The presented beamforming architecture has been optimized to produce relative delay ranging from −600 psec to +600 psec and the antenna array has intentionally configured to produce multiple beams in different directions.

articleTitle: Non-contact Fatigue Driving Detection Using CW Doppler Radar
abstract: This paper presents a non-contact fatigue driving monitoring method using the continuous-wave (CW) Doppler radar. The driver's breathing and heartbeat signals can be measured by the Doppler radar located at the car instrument panel. Then seven features in the time-domain and frequency-domain are extracted from the received signal. Extensive experiments are conducted to collect 240 observations from three healthy volunteers. Finally, a decision tree based on detection algorithm is realized to achieve the accuracy rate of 82.5%, which demonstrates the feasibility of the proposed method for fatigue driving monitoring.

articleTitle: A dimension-reduced artificial neural network for the compact modeling of semiconductor devices
abstract: A dimension-reduced artificial neural network (DRANN) is proposed for the compact modeling of semiconductor devices. The fully connected feedforward artificial neural network (FFANN) is known for its universal fitting ability, however, measurement data are usually not sufficient to train the FFANN, for example, semiconductor devices are commonly measured under limited (2 or 3) ambient temperatures, which will cause overfitting problem if temperature is directly taken as the input of FFANN. In this paper, DRANN is proposed to address the overfitting problem for multi-dimensional data mapping. The dimensions (such as port voltages) with enough datasets are modeled by FFANN, whilst other dimensions (such as thermal and traps) with few datasets are represented by Taylor expansion. DRANN is finally a combination of multiple low-dimensional FFANNs. The DRANN is verified by the accurate prediction of pulsed I-Vs (PIVs) of GaN HEMT with various thermal and trap states.

articleTitle: On-chip reconfigurable reflectarray for 2-D beam-steering at W-band
abstract: In this paper, a on-chip reconfigurable reflectarray (RRA) for 2-D beam-steering at W-band is designed, fabricated and tested. Beam steering can be realized by RRA, with the ability of shifting reflective phase by integrating tunable devices. In our work, the GaAs based chip process is used for a RRA integrated with p-i-n diode at W-band, to guarantee precision and improve flexibility. One 16×16 RRA prototype at W-band with each elements individually in control is fabricated at W-band. The beam steering is experimentally demonstrated using a near-field measurement system, showing ±10° beam steering in E-plane and 10° beam steering in H-plane.

articleTitle: A novel quadruple-mode cavity resonator filter with wide spurious-free window
abstract: This paper proposes a novel quadruple-mode cavity resonator and filter. The cavity resonator includes four modes which are similar in frequency and easily controlled, and 20% volume saving can be achieved while maintaining the similar unloaded Q-factor value of the conventional designs. Furthermore, the electric field of the proposed modes is mainly composed of horizontal components, so the four modes can be simulated by using a pair of coupling probes, and the wide spurious-free window is realized. In final, to demonstrate the new resonator technology, a four-pole filter with 40 MHz wide filter at 2.56GHz is simulated and fabricated, and the measured S-parameter frequency response have demonstrated the significant improvement in spurious performance.

articleTitle: A compact E-shaped half-mode substrate integrated waveguide semi-circular antenna
abstract: A novel compact E-shaped half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) semi-circular antenna is put forward in this paper. Two symmetrical slots are inserted into HMSIW semi-circular antenna to decrease the operating frequency of the antenna. The slot helps to meander the current in cavity and radiate below resonant frequency. A semi-circular cavity is implemented to reduce the size of the antenna. A fabricated prototype is presented and realizes a maximum gain of 4.6 dB over the bandwidth of 80 MHz (1%). This antenna possesses a good performance with low profile, 15 dB front-to-back ratio, and cross-polarization level below -15dB.

articleTitle: Wideband microwave photonic I/Q mixer based on parallel installed phase modulator and Mach-Zehnder modulator
abstract: A wideband microwave photonic in-phase and quadrature (I/Q) mixer is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. In the proposed system, the 90-degree phase difference of the I/Q mixer is achieved by implementing phase modulation and intensity modulation in I and Q channels, respectively. Experimental results show that the proposed I/Q mixer has the advantages of excellent 90-degree phase balance (<;±3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>) and a small amplitude imbalance less than 1 dB in a wide radio-frequency bandwidth from 10 to 36 GHz.

articleTitle: Cross-shaped PnC for anchor loss reduction of thin-film ALN-on-silicon high frequency MEMS resonator
abstract: This paper presents an approach to reduce the anchor loss of thin-film-piezoelectric-on-silicon (TPoS) high frequency MEMS resonator. The PnC prevents acoustic wave to propagate through the support tethers, and reflects it back to the resonator body, which serves to increase the store energy, and then enhances the quality factor (Q). This design discussed the effect of the tether width, tether length, and impact of the design geometry on bandgap and the quality factor. The desired design of PnCs provides wide bandgap and high quality factor by introducing cross-shaped of 2D phononic crystal externally on anchors. The design provides a bandgap up to 230MHz and increases the quality factor from 21,180 to 221,536. The technique provides a high quality factor than the previous work.

articleTitle: Wideband power divider using double-layer periodic spoof surface plasmon polaritons
abstract: In this paper, a wideband power divider using single- and double-layer periodic spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) is proposed. Double-sided parallel-strip line (DSPSL) is used to realize the wideband and low loss for the double-layer spoof SPPs. T-shaped spoof SPPs power dividers with large bandwidth, wideband isolation and low loss using double-layer spoof SPPs to single-layer spoof SPPs transition are realized. Conventional coplanar waveguide (CPW) is used as the output ports for the single-layer spoof SPPs. Good agreements can be observed between the measured and simulated results, indicating good potential applications in the integrated plasmonic devices.

articleTitle: High-gain and low-profile microstrip antenna using slot-loaded TM50 mode
abstract: This paper presents a high-gain and low-profile microstrip antenna with single-layered substrate. The proposed antenna consists of a rectangular patch, which operates in higher order TM50 mode, and two identical slots etched on the patch. A four-element equivalent magnetic current array is constructed within a single cavity, including two from the radiating aperture of the patch and another two from the etched slots. Only one substrate layer and single feed are used here with the merits of low profile and simple feeding. High gain, e.g., 3 dB higher than conventional microstrip antenna operating in the fundamental mode, is obtained from the single-layered structure. The measured gain of 11.3 dBi is achieved with the antenna profile of 0.027λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the free-space wavelength of operating frequency), agreeing well with the simulations. The proposed antenna has the advantages of high gain, low profile, single feeding and low cost, with great potential in designing dual-polarized microstrip antennas and arrays with larger scale.

articleTitle: Propagation range enhancement of truncated airy beam with antenna array at microwave frequencies
abstract: In order to improve wireless power transmission efficiency which is largely influenced by the diffraction of transmission beam, the use of quasi-diffraction-free beam, and, in particular, the Airy beam, is considered. Therefore the objective of this work is to investigate the generation of an Airy beam at microwave frequencies with antenna arrays when the quasi-diffraction-free requirement is limited to a specific distance along with the propagation axis. In this case, it is observed that the emission aperture can be opportunely truncated in order to observe an Airy distribution at the specified distance and within a specific observation region. Furthermore, microstrip patch antennas instead of simple dipoles are employed to increase the range of the Airy beam generation, and different array inter-element spaces are compared for evaluating the beam energy decay along with the longitudinal distance.

articleTitle: Characterization of damper-to-damper wireless channel in small cars
abstract: The increasing use of Intra-Vehicular Wireless Sensor Networks (IVWSNs) in smart cars has enabled advances on Intelligent Transportation System (ITS) and also extended electric cars driving range by reducing cable weight. Intra-vehicular wireless systems have been characterized at 2.4 GHz and UHF bands. However, works on channel characterization of damper-to-damper wireless systems are still limited. This paper presents a damper-to-damper path loss characterization at 2.4 GHz frequency band for small cars. Dynamic on-field measurements on damper-to-damper antennas are used to derive path loss specification and coherence bandwidth for an intra-vehicular wireless communication system. Static measurements show the impact of antenna polarization in damper-to-damper path loss.

articleTitle: High-rejection wideband bandstop filter with good frequency selectivity
abstract: In this paper, a brand-new wideband bandstop filter with good frequency selectivity is proposed. The wideband bandstop response with five transmission zeros and high stopband rejection is implemented using the modified coupled-line sections. The transmission zeros and poles are derived based on even- and odd-mode analysis. For demonstration, a design prototype operating at 2 GHz with 79.5% relative bandwidth of 35-dB stopband rejection is simulated, fabricated, and measured. Good agreements between simulated and measured results can be observed.

articleTitle: Transducer gain maximization for a resonant inductive WPT link using relay resonators
abstract: This paper analyzes a resonant inductive Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) link using relay elements (i.e., additional resonators not directly connected to either the source or the load). Two different cases are analyzed and compared: the case of a link using one single relay element and the case of a link using two relay elements. The transducer gain as defined in the context of active two-port networks is adopted for evaluating the performance of the link.

articleTitle: A design of high-gain vivaldi antenna loaded with antipodal structure and slotting correction
abstract: Vivaldi antenna, a kind of tapered slot antenna, is widely used in the design of planar ultra wideband antennas. Vivaldi antennas can broaden the bandwidth infinitely in theory, but the improvement of the gain is not prominent because of the processing technology and dimension. This letter loads the antipodal structure on the front of the radiation structure. The results indicate that the relative bandwidth broadens by 79.1% and the gain increases 3 dBi at 5.5 GHz and 12 GHz. The technology of slotting correction makes the radiation phrase distribution more symmetrical, enhancing the efficiency of the amplitude distribution. The results indicate that the gain increases 2 dBi through loading the slotting correction. Both of the technology in the design performs high gain, simple design and miniaturization, which provides a new idea for high-gain antenna design and applications in ultra-wideband antenna fields.

articleTitle: Dual-band dual-polarized transmitarray for satellite communications
abstract: A novel dual-band and dual-polarized transmitarray is proposed for both downlink and uplink frequency bands (12.5/14.25 GHz) of satellite communications. Two 3-layer elements are interlaced in a unit cell for dual-band operation, which achieves more than 300° phase range independently with less than 2 dB insertion loss in both bands. The dual-band transmitarray has achieved high gains of 31.3 dBi and 32.4 dBi with aperture efficiencies of 46.5% and 47.3% in downlink and uplink frequency bands respectively.

articleTitle: A dual-polarized antenna with pattern diversity based on a two-mode single-layer microstrip patch
abstract: A dual-polarized single-layer circular microstrip patch antenna with pattern diversity is designed, analyzed and tested. The developed two-port antenna can provide two orthogonal polarization radiations including one patch-like pattern of mode TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> and one monopole-like pattern of mode TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</sub>. To make the two modes work at the same frequency band, the circular patch is shorted concentrically by a set of conductive vias. The developed antenna works at 3.5 GHz having a compact structure with a low profile of 0.035 wavelengths. The measured -10 dB reflection coefficient bandwidth of the two radiation patterns are 3.46-3.57 GHz and 3.41-3.61 GHz, respectively. Simulation results of the S parameters and radiation patterns are presented and validated by experimental measurements.

articleTitle: A VCO-dedicated digital LDO with multi-comparator coarse loop and 1-bit ΔΣ fine loop for robust frequency generation
abstract: This paper describes a fully integrated two-stage digital low-dropout regulator (DLDO) architecture for robust frequency generation under low supply voltage. The DLDO designed for a voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) in the phase-locked loop (PLL) provides constant or temperature-compensated supply voltage with a 1-bit ΔΣ modulated fine loop, while offering fast transient performance over load current jump with the multi-comparator coarse loop. The proposed DLDO designed in 65nm CMOS generates a noise-shaped output whose peak value is less than 1mV with a 200pF on-chip capacitor. The low dropout voltage of 50mV from a 1.0V supply is achieved with the load current ranging from 2.0μA to 13.0mA.

articleTitle: The terahertz radiometer for APSOS project at Yangbajing Observing Station
abstract: A dual-band SIS terahertz heterodyne spectrometer for Atmospheric Profiling Synthetic Observation System (APSOS) project has been designed and is now operating in Yangbajing Observing Station, Tibet. It aims at observing the spectral lines of greenhouse gas as well as monitoring the local atmospheric opacity at the frequency range of 180~380 GHz. The architecture of the spectrometer has been described in detail. The measured receiver system noise is less than 160K at 180~300GHz and less than 230K at 320~380GHz. The measurement theory and method of atmospheric opacity and spectral lines has been described, and ozone molecular spectral lines have been preliminary observed.

articleTitle: An indoor FMCW localization system with the application of the extended Kalman filter
abstract: This paper presents a device-free indoor localization system using frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) technology. The system localizes a target by using the two round-trip distances obtained with the two R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>-T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> links. To improve the accuracy, a frequency correction approach is proposed and the extended Kalman filter is applied to track a target. Experiments were conducted to demonstrate the validity of the proposed system and method. Future directions in further improvement of the locating accuracy are presented.

articleTitle: Triple-mode wideband bandpass filter using triangular waveguide cavity
abstract: This paper presents the realization of a triple-mode wideband bandpass filter, by inserting a metallic cylinder and a pin along with two coaxial probes for perturbation using an equilateral triangular waveguide cavity. A TM mode along with two degenerate hybrid modes namely HE+ and HE-, are excited by the simple perturbation in a single triangular metal cavity. The filter operates at central frequency of 2.94 GHz with fractional bandwidth of 22%. The computer aided design of the filter is simulated for S-parameters, showing satisfactory results.

articleTitle: Full integration of physics-based propagation models into network protocol design for communication-based train control systems
abstract: Communication-based train control (CBTC) systems are new generation rail signaling systems, aimed at achieving train control through wireless communication between the train and a network of access points (APs). The performance of CBTC systems rely significantly on the AP deployment. Previous studies have focused on optimizing AP locations based on received signal strength (RSS). This paper extends this paradigm to evaluate the effect of a given set of AP locations on network protocol design. This approach paves the way for the integration of physics-based optimization and network design for train communication systems by providing insights for further AP optimizations.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of frequency characteristics of underwater wireless power transfer
abstract: Frequency characteristics of underwater wireless power transfer systems centered at 470 kHz are investigated experimentally. Experimental results show the V-type frequency splitting pattern disappears in seawater and freshwater. When the coil distance is bigger than the 22.5 cm coil diameter (the midrange conception), the eddy current behaves like a relay coil, the load voltage is stable at 6 V in seawater and at 5 V in fresh-water and insensitive to the coil distance while it is decayed exponentially to 0.2 V in air.

articleTitle: K-band combined GaAs monolithic Doherty power amplifier
abstract: This paper presents the design, simulations, and measurements of a 35 dBm K-band Doherty power amplifier, fabricated on 0.15μm GaAs monolithic technology of Qorvo. The power amplifier is based on combining on-chip two Doherty modules with a matching power combiner. To demonstrate the power scaling and gain a better insight into the design, the single Doherty module has been fabricated and characterized as well. The Doherty output matching is designed for maximizing the bandwidth and minimizing the components count, with the output capacitance of the active devices determining the impedance inverter impedance. The combined Doherty shows an output power of 35 dBm at 24 GHz, that is almost exactly 3 dB larger than the single Doherty module power module, and with a 6 dB OBO efficiency of 27%, and a gain of 11.5dB. It compares well with the state of the art, representing the highest power GaAs Doherty at similar frequencies.

articleTitle: Kurtosis CFAR detection for indoor positioning applications with FMCW systems
abstract: Frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar technique has been widely used in tracking system, e.g., WiTrack System. In this paper, based on fourth order statistic, i.e., Kurtosis (KD), we propose a non-coherent CFAR detection method for FMCW indoor positioning. We develop mathematical model, investigate impacts of parameters and conduct performance evaluations. Our results show the proposed Kurtosis based detection outperforms the conventional FMCW detection technique under additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN), line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight channel conditions. The detection probability with the proposed method can be twice better than the conventional method.

articleTitle: Filtering power divider with high selectivity using modified coupled-line bandpass filter
abstract: This letter presents a filtering power divider using modified parallel coupled-line bandpass filter (BPF) with multiple coupling from source/load to resonators. This novel coupling topology includes additional coupling between source/load and non-adjacent resonators, namely, extra cross-coupling paths, for a better selectivity. Then less resonators are required to achieve the same stopband performance compared with conventional parallel coupled-line BPF with the same order. Three isolation resistors, instead of only one in the conventional power dividers, are used for flexible optimization of isolation. For validation, a three-order filtering power divider operating at 3.4 GHz is demonstrated with more than 14 dB in-band isolation. Three transmission zeros are generated at 2.02 GHz, 2.56 GHz and 4.34 GHz to achieve a better selectivity.

articleTitle: A new multi-band Gysel power divider
abstract: In this paper, a new multi-band Gysel power divider (PD) is proposed. Compared with the conventional Gysel PD, two additional multi-band biasing networks composed of trunk transmission lines (TLs) and shunted open-end stubs are attached with the phase inverters between the two isolation resistors. Besides multiple passbands, this configuration also results in simple structure without additional via holes or lumped elements. In addition, just like as the traditional Gysel PD, the proposed one also features high-power handling capability, and higher working frequencies than Wilkinson PDs, which makes it more suitable for the application of 5G mobile communication. Detailed closed-form design equations are derived and verified by a tri-band design operating at 2.0 GHz, 2.5 GHz, and 3.0 GHz.

articleTitle: K-band liquid-crystal-based frequency and pattern reconfigurable linear antenna array
abstract: A K-band Liquid-crystal-based frequency and pattern reconfigurable antenna array is proposed in this paper, there are two layers of liquid crystal material in the geometrical model of the antenna array, one of which is used to dynamically tune the operation frequency of the antenna array while the other one is used to achieve beam steering. The simulation results show that the antenna array works in a bandwidth of 500MHz, and its center operation frequency moves from 22.4GHz to 23.3GHz with the peak gain which is larger than 8.5dBi. When working in a certain center operation frequency, the antenna array realized a 20° beam scanning.

articleTitle: An X-band low voltage cross-coupled voltage-controlled oscillator IC in 56-nm SOI CMOS
abstract: An X-band voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) IC is presented in this paper for low voltage operation. The LC-VCO IC consists of a cross-coupled pMOSFET pair, an LC tank circuit and buffer amplifiers. The LC-VCO IC is designed, fabricated and fully evaluated on-wafer using 56-nm SOI CMOS technology. The fabricated VCO IC has exhibited a measured phase noise of -119.02 dBc/Hz at 5 MHz offset from the 9.8 GHz carrier frequency at an operation voltage of only 0.5 V.

articleTitle: A dual-band Quasi-Yagi wearable antenna with high directivity
abstract: A Quasi-Yagi wearable antenna is presented in this paper for dual-band operations at WiFi bands with high individual directivities. The proposed antenna structure consists of a single-stage director, two arms of driven elements and a concave parabolic reflector. The measurement results show a directivity of 6.8 dBi with 12% bandwidth at 2.45 GHz and a directivity of 5.3 dBi with 10% bandwidth at 5 GHz, respectively. Both the lower band and the higher band can be tuned by changing the length of the two driven arms with stable radiation patterns. The size of this dual-band antenna is only 55 mm × 48 mm × 0.25 mm. The proposed antenna is promising for the applications of both wireless power transfer and wireless communication for wearable devices.

articleTitle: Multi-band reflectionless filtering impedance transformers
abstract: A type of double-functionality filtering impedance transformer with multi-band and input-reflectionless capabilities is presented. It exploits a multi-passband filtering/impedance-transformation channel loaded with a complementary resistively-terminated multi-bandstop branch at its input node that dissipates the input-signal energy in the stopband regions of the former. This multi-band/multi-operational circuit approach could result in insertion-loss and circuit-size advantages when employed in complete RF front-end chains by relaxing the need for isolators or attenuators for inter-block matching. A coupling-matrix-based formulation for its design and theoretical examples of first-order dual-band and second-order triple-band realizations are provided. Furthermore, for experimental-demonstration purposes, a 1.9/2.1-GHz dual-band microstrip prototype is built and tested.

articleTitle: Low-profile highly-selective absorptive frequency selective transmission structure
abstract: A novel absorptive frequency selective transmission structure (AFST) with one highly-selective passband within the absorption bands is presented. By cascading one lossy layer and one lossless layer, one highly selective passband between two absorption bands is obtained. The lossy layer consists of stub resonators, while the lossless layer is composed of cross-frame slot array. Under normal incidence, the proposed structure features insertion loss of 0.32 dB at 4.3 GHz, the fractional bandwidth is 111.3% for reflection less than -10 dB, while the thickness is only 0.09 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> at the lowest absorption frequency.

articleTitle: Conjugate image impedance matching for maximizing the gains of a WPT link
abstract: This paper focuses on the use of appropriate matching networks for resonant inductive Wireless Power Transfer (WPT). The link is described by using the power gain definitions commonly adopted for active networks. It is theoretically and experimentally demonstrated that the use of adaptive networks realizing the conjugate image impedance matching condition allows maximizing the three gains for variable values of the coupling coefficient.

articleTitle: An indoor multipath-assisted single-anchor UWB localization method
abstract: In this paper, an indoor Ultra Wide Band (U localization system relying on a single-anchor setup is prese Conventional UWB localization systems require at least i anchors for trilateration, which leads to high system complexity and cost. Hence new technologies, such as the Virtual An (VA) approach are emerging to achieve single-anchor localiza The VA concept models Multipath Components (MPCs individual distance measurements thus exploiting reflections the environment to aid the accuracy of the localization. Exi single-anchor approaches require a priori information of pre” tag positions to estimate the current tag position. The novelty of this paper is an initialization method that enables estimate tag position without the use of a priori position information. The proposed solution is validated using both simulations and measurements. Both simulations and measurements have shown positive results, which indicates that single-anchor location is feasible.

articleTitle: Reflective phase-shifting surface for generating orbital angular momentum waves
abstract: In this paper, a circular polarized reflective phase-shifting surface which consists of 20×20 elements is designed to generate orbital angular momentum (OAM) waves at 6 GHz. The phase-shifting surface is composed of a substrate with split-rings printed on the top surface, an air layer and a metal ground. Using proposed reflective phase-shifting surface, OAM wave with mode 1 is achieved and its phase and magnitude distributions of E-fleld in far field are analyzed. The results show that the OAM beam purity of the reflective beam with mode 1 can reach around 96%, and the maximum gain is 22.0 dBi at 6 GHz.

articleTitle: A cavity-backed end-fire dipole antenna using SISL technology for 24 GHz automotive anti-collision radar system
abstract: This paper presents a cavity-backed dipole antenna based on substrate-integrated suspended line (SISL) platform. By utilizing the double side substrate-integrated suspended line (DSISL) feeding network, the substrate and radiation loss are significantly decreased, thus efficiency of better than 95.50% is achieved. The proposed antenna obtained the measured 10 dB impedance bandwidth of 7.18 GHz, i.e., from 21.75 to 28.93 GHz, which covers the 24.25-26.65 GHz automotive anti-collision radar system band. Moreover, the proposed antenna can be fabricated by conventional printed circuit board (PCB) process, and it can be easily integrated with other planar circuit and applied in the 24-GHz radar system.

articleTitle: Evaluation of knee voltage effect and soft turn-on characteristic on the load modulated continuous class-B/J power amplifier
abstract: The impact of knee voltage effect and soft turn-on characteristic of the practical transistor on the design space of load modulated (LM) continuous Class-B/J power amplifiers (PAs) is analyzed and improved design space is proposed in this paper. For LM continuous Class-B/J PAs with a practical transistor, the knee voltage effect has a noticeable effect on the dynamic load-lines when the dynamic load modulation at the current generator plane (CGP) is proceeding. The chosen load impedance of LM continuous Class-B/J PAs with optimum output power and efficiency at the 0 dB output power back-off (OPBO) can be affected by the knee voltage effect. The soft turn-on characteristic can lead to a non-null drain quiescent current at Class-B/J mode, which limits the dynamic OPBO range with high efficiency. Based on the Pedro load-line theory, the improved design space of LM continuous Class-B/J PAs can offer a more accurate prediction on the efficiency contours and provide more effective theory guidance in designing high-efficiency LM PAs.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband (UWB) phase shifter on multimode resonator: Concept, theory, and design
abstract: In this paper, a new universal design method of ultra-wideband (UWB) phase shifter on multimode resonators (MMR) is proposed and developed. The generalized topology of proposed phase shifters based on MMR is presented and their phase properties with J and K inverters are both analyzed. On the one hand, the phase shift performances are found dominated by the excitation of resonant modes, regardless of J and K inverters. On the other hand, the proposed 45° and 90° phase shifters can easily obtain bandwidth more than 110% with simple geometry and single-layer structure compared with other reported designs. The working principle and design method are given. Meanwhile, theoretical analysis of magnitude and phase shift bandwidth are carried out. Finally, a prototype of 90° phase shifter is fabricated and tested. The measured results well verify our design concept.

articleTitle: Printed spiral coils with multiloop technique for planar magnetically coupled resonant wireless power transfer system
abstract: In this paper, a planar magnetically coupled resonant wireless power transfer (MCR-WPT) system is proposed to achieve high efficiency over a distance by using printed spiral coils with multiloop technique. The multiloop technique of applying several loops with different sizes allows the adjustment of the coupling coefficient depending on the distance between the transmitter and the receiver. It enables the optimum efficiency to be obtained where one of the three loops is selected. The fabricated MCR-WPT system maintains high efficiency across a range of 0–25cm. The efficiency is 46.2% at a distance of 25cm, which is 36% higher than the conventional system. The maximum efficiency is 88.7% at a distance of 10cm.

articleTitle: Dual-band and dual-polarized repeater antenna for wearable applications
abstract: A novel dual-band repeater antenna is presented for wearable applications in this paper, covering 2.45 GHz (2.4-2.485 GHz) and 5.8 GHz (5.725-5.875 GHz) industrial scientific medical (ISM) bands. By utilizing stacked structure, different polarization properties are achieved at two bands for the proposed antenna. At 2.45 GHz ISM band, circular polarization property is achieved by adopting a truncated patch at the bottom layer, meeting the demands of communication with implants. While at 5.8 GHz ISM band intended for off-body communication, shorted circular patch is introduced, forming a monopole-like radiation pattern with linear polarization property.

articleTitle: Near-field focused reflectarray antenna at 140 GHz
abstract: A kind of reflectarray antenna with the characteristics of near-field focusing at 140 GHz is investigated in this paper. The element is a cross-shaped structure, which is implemented on the TLY-5 substrate and fabricated by the PCB technology. A pyramidal horn is used to feed the reflectarray. In this design, numerical simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the radiated electromagnetic power can be focused in a fixed target area. Such a near-field characteristic of the proposed re-flectarray can be a feasible candidate for the Terahertz imaging and detection in the future research.

articleTitle: A planar balanced branch-line coupler with filtering function
abstract: A planar balanced branch-line coupler with filtering function is proposed, which is realized by four quarter-wavelength microstrip lines and eight quarter-wavelength coupled lines. The proposed design not only exhibits the functions of power dividing and filtering for differential-mode signal, but also can suppress the common-mode signal. Furthermore, the proposed planar design is easy to process when compared with the reported double-layer balanced filtering branch-line coupler. The measured results show the insertion loss of 2.1 dB at 1.7 GHz, the 3-dB bandwidth of 5.6%, the isolation better than 15 dB from 1.65 to 2.03 GHz, and the common-mode suppression higher than 20 dB from 1.64 to 2.01 GHz.

articleTitle: A novel terahertz phased array based on coupled oscillators
abstract: In this paper, a novel phased array based on coupled oscillators in loop structure for 1D phased array is proposed. By controlling the coupling phase in the oscillators array, initial stable modes are split so that a continuous fixed phase difference from -180° to 180° between adjacent oscillators have been achieved. A complete design methodology is introduced to implement arbitrary desired phase difference in the array. The system is demonstrated in 200GHz and perturbation recovery time is less than 100ns.

articleTitle: Multigain cascode technique for low power BLE ISM band 2.4GHz differential inductive source degeneration based LNA
abstract: This paper presents the design & simulations of CMOS Multigain low noise amplifier (LNA) for wireless applications, specific for (ISM) band 2.4 GHz Low Energy Bluetooth (BLE). The proposed structure is implemented using an inductive source degeneration technique, multi-cascode, differential structure and modified LC NMOS varactor based output matching with multiplex register control and data-path interconnect to get minimum in band ripples. The simulations were made using Cadence Virtuoso IC Design. The proposed work emphasized on the multigain, low in band ripples, and the LC NMOS varactor based output matching.

articleTitle: High efficiency triple-stacked class-E power amplifier with novel dynamic biasing network
abstract: In this paper, we present a 5-GHz high efficiency class-E power amplifier. Due to zero voltage switching and zero voltage derivative switching conditions, class-E power amplifiers (PAs) are highly efficient. But the reliability of device caused by excessively high peak voltages should be considered carefully. In order to alleviate the device stress, a triple-stacked class-E PA with proposed dynamic biasing network is presented, which can divide the voltage stress equally among three transistors. The supply voltage of the proposed PA is increased compared to common source or cascode class-E PA, which enhances the efficiency of class-E PA. Because of the high supply voltage and operating frequency of 5 GHz, the proposed class-E PA requires small shunt capacitance, which limits the transistor size. The proposed parallel resonant inductor breaks this limitation and avoids the power loss caused by the large on-resistance of small-sized transistors. The proposed PA is implemented in a 0.18 μm CMOS process with the chip area of 0.235 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Simulation results show that the PA achieves 49.5% power-added efficiency (PAE) and 53.7% drain efficiency while delivering peak output power of 22.3 dBm at 5 GHz.

articleTitle: High efficiency and wideband hybrid envelope amplifier for envelope tracking operation of wireless transmitter
abstract: This paper presents a high performance Envelope Amplifier (EA) whose architecture includes a linear stage in conjunction with a switching buck converter (switcher stage). This hybrid configuration provides high efficiency and high linearity for the wideband signal. Using a 10MHz 6.6dB peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) LTE signal, the proposed hybrid EA circuit achieves an efficiency of 83.7% at the average output power of 13.2W driving a 8Ω resistive load, and the gain of the EA circuit can be maintained at around 11 (20.8dB). In order to evaluate the application of the envelope amplifier, the whole ET system is set up for testing. Measurement results show that the ET power amplifier improves PAE by 10% at an average output power of 35.6dBm (6 dB back off point) with respect to fixed supply power amplifier, and the ACPR1 of this ET Transmitter is less than −50 dBc with digital pre-distortion (DPD) technique.

articleTitle: Design of N-way high power combiner based on E-plane stepped waveguide T-junction
abstract: In this paper, a design method of N-way high power combiner based on E-plane stepped waveguide T-junction is introduced in detail. The equivalent characteristic impedance and discontinuity of E-plane stepped waveguide T-junction are analyzed theoretically. Based on the above analysis results, this paper presents a design scheme of 6-way high power combiner with UHF band. The combiner's rated input power and total output power are 20kw and 120kw respectively. The HFSS software is used for modeling and simulation, and the simulation results verify the correctness and validity of the design scheme.

articleTitle: A novel single-fed high-gain and phase-adjustable transmitting antenna element for wireless power transmission
abstract: A novel single-fed high-gain and phase-adjustable cavity slot antenna element is presented in this paper. The antenna consists of a slotted cavity cover, a driven dipole and a polarization twist reflector. And a 2×4 slots array is etched on the top surface of the cavity cover. To excite the cavity slots with uniform amplitude and phase, the polarization twist reflector is used here. Thus, the antenna can achieve the high-gain property. In addition, by rotating the polarization of the driven dipole, the antenna can provide a continuous and linear phase in the far-field region. With the phase-adjustable property, the element can be regarded as an integration of a high-gain antenna and a phase shifter, which is a favorable feature for a phased array. The proposed antenna element is fabricated and can achieve an impedance bandwidth of 2.1%. Within the bandwidth, the measured maximum gain and radiation efficiency are 13.6 dBi and 93%, respectively. Additionally, under the constrains of 1-dB gain drop and VSWR ≤ 2.0, a continuous and linear phase change from 0° to 40.2° at 5.8 GHz is obtained.

articleTitle: A novel CPW-SIW filter with wide stopband performance
abstract: In this paper, a novel planar bandpass filter with wide stopband suppression is proposed based on the combination of coplanar waveguide (CPW) and substrate integrated wave-guide (SIW) technologies. The wide stopband suppression is achieved by eliminating the second harmonic resonance of the CPW cavity with a centrally positioned metallic via, which plays a key role in the novel design. The proposed filter could obtain good out-of-band rejection (<;-20 dB) from 18 GHz (1.5 f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>)is the center operating frequency of the filter) to 43 GHz (3.6/o). A demonstration filter is optimized, fabricated and measured, and the measured results agree well with the simulated ones, which validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: An improved sub-threshold swing model for MIT virtual source GaN model
abstract: In this paper, the derivation of sub-threshold swing in the MIT model and its relationship to punch through factor are introduced. Then, an improved model of sub-threshold swing implementing the Fermi function in punch through factor is proposed. The improved model can well characterize both the linear and saturation behavior of sub-threshold swing in medium and high drain-to-source voltage regions respectively. Benchmarking results regarding sub-threshold swing performance and its impact on drain current in sub-threshold region are presented to validate this improved model.

articleTitle: Interconnect reliability analysis for a 26–40 GHz 1-watt stacked GaAs pHEMT power amplifier design
abstract: Using the finite element analysis (FEA) for the atomic flux divergence (AFD) analysis, the prediction of interconnect reliability for a stacked power amplifier (PA) is achieved effectively to learn the electro-migration (EM) failure of interconnect. As a circuit example, a Ka band PA is designed using a 0.1 μm GaAs pHEMT process, which employs a 3-stacked-FET to obtain about 1-watt output power with corresponding power added efficiency (PAE) of 30-37.4% within a very small chip size of 1.4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This is the first time to analyze the interconnect reliability for the s tacked MMIC PA, which can help the designers to find the weakest spot for the stacked PA and give some important guidance for PA reliability design.

articleTitle: High-Q dual-band EBG filter with two independently tunable passbands
abstract: A novel design for compact tunable dual-band EBG (Electromagnetic Bandgap) filter is proposed. The tunable filter is implemented in RO4350 substrate using PCB (Printed Circuit Board) process with surface mounted solid-state varactors and lumped capacitors. The filter is unique that by sharing same substrate and surrounding posts, tunable dual-band filter can be achieved in a compact size with good band to band isolation and wide spurious free region. Besides, frequencies of dual passbands can be independently tuned to customizable selected frequencies by changing applied DC voltage of varactors. Finally, the simulated and measured results of the filter are found in good agreement.

articleTitle: CMOS circuit techniques for mm-wave communications
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mm-wave) communication has drawn much attention due to up to 10Gbps data rate potential. Along with its rapid development, CMOS process has become promising for low cost mm-wave communication chips, even though great challenges still exist. In this paper, the challenges on the circuit implementation techniques in CMOS process for mm-wave communications have been discussed and possible solutions are overviewed, based on our recent research work.

articleTitle: A GNU radio based FMCW radar with a simple frequency correction technique for accurate indoor localization applications
abstract: Frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radars have been widely used for measuring target range and speed. In this paper, we investigate and analyze its performances for indoor localization application. We develop a simple method to correct errors in finding beat frequency and present a two-step process to reduce background reflections from stationary objects. We use Matlab Simulink for simulations and employ USRP and GNU Radio platforms to construct a FMCW test setup. Both simulations and experimental results show the proposed method improve accuracy by 1.6 to 18 times over the conventional method.

articleTitle: A two-dimensional beam-switchable patch array antenna with polarization-diversity for 5G applications
abstract: A compact multi-beam 2×2 patch array antenna, with the ability of switching the radiation beam and polarization, is presented. Each element antenna has two sets of perturbation segments for circular polarization agility and three switchable feeding probes, which are integrated with a designed single-pole triple-throw (SPTT) switch. The phase distribution required for different radiation beams is realized by selecting proper feeding probes for each element antenna. The array antenna is capable of simultaneously switching the radiation beams among nine different directions and reconfiguring the polarization between two orthogonal circular polarization states with an enhanced 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth.

articleTitle: A 173 GHz transformer-based push-push oscillator with 11.2% tuning range in 28nm CMOS
abstract: This paper presents a transformer-based push-push oscillator for the terahertz (THz) frequency generation with a wideband operation. Transformer-based oscillator is implemented carefully to extend the tuning range and improve the phase noise performance, simultaneously. Center-taps of two stages in transformer are combined to generate the push-push output signal.
