A floating-ground shield structure is utilized and located under the transformer to improve the quality-factor, which reduces the substrate coupling effect and transformer size. The THz oscillator is fabricated in a conventional 28nm CMOS process with a compact core size of 0.01 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Measurement results exhibit the 11.2% frequency tuning range from 163.2 to 182.6 GHz and phase noise of -100.5 dBc/Hz at 10 MHz offset of a carrier at 182.6 GHz. The corresponding F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub> is 170 dBc/Hz.

articleTitle: Cross polarization conversion and RCS reduction using venus-like metallic resonators
abstract: This paper presents the design of low backscattered non-absorptive reflective surface at W-band. The presented non-absorptive reflective surface is designed based on cross-polarization conversion principle in which a simple geometry copper unit cell of Venus-like shape is used to compose the surface. The unit cell has three plasmon resonance frequencies at about 96GHz, 97.4GHz, and 99GHz. The unit cell can convert the incident x-or y-polarized EM-waves to their orthogonal components with more than 90% cross-polarization conversion efficiency from about 95.7GHz to 99.3GHz. Moreover, if the proposed unit cell along with its mirrored unit cell are precisely designed and randomly distributed across the surface aperture and arranged in 2D lattice, then 180<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>±30<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> of reflection phase difference (cancellation) is valid and a low-level backscattered diffuse radar cross sction patterns can be obtained.

articleTitle: Mode composite waveguide directional coupler
abstract: In this work, a mode composite waveguide (MCW) directional coupler is proposed and demonstrated. Due to the dual mode nature of the MCW, the mode conversion between the inner and outer waveguide is involved during power coupling. The coupler operation principle is mathematically formulated in achieving the required power summation and cancellation, and a detailed design methodology is also presented. An MCW backward directional coupler at 10 GHz is fabricated to validate the proposed concept. The desired coupling level of -20 dB and the maximum isolation of -50 dB are obtained in the coupler measurement.

articleTitle: A 21.5–26.4 GHz CMOS cascode driver amplifier with 13.9 dBm output power for 24G FMCW radar applications
abstract: This paper presents a 21.5–26.4 GHz CMOS cascode driver amplifier (DA) for 24G radar applications. The two stacked cascode configuration can provide enough output power and power gain under the limitation of low gate-oxide breakdown voltage and low drain-source reach-through voltage, ensuring the reliability of long-term work. Reasonably taking advantage of the virtual ground of the differential structure helps to achieve a compact layout without degrading performance. It is fabricated in 65 nm CMOS with a core chip area of 0.3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(600 μm × 500 μm). At 24 GHz, the measurement results demonstrate the DA delivers saturated output power (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf>)of 13.9 dBm, output 1 dB compression point (OP1dB) of 9.02 dBm, with a peak PAE of 20 % and gain of 23.6 dB. From 21 to 26 GHz, the DA achieves OP1dB lager than 9 dBm.

articleTitle: A millimeter-wave Doppler sensor for bio-signals detection
abstract: In this paper, we report a single-board integrated Doppler radar system (DRS) operating at 24 GHz. To verify the performance of the 24-GHz DRS, we make a comparison between the existing 5.8-GHz Doppler radar system (DRS) and the 24-GHz one about the ability to detect the bio-signals (heartbeats, respiration and human gait). In the experiment, DRSs are placed in the same experimental environment and working at the same time for the comparison purposes. Experimental results show that the 24-GHz DRS detects Doppler bio-signals of both the small-scale human cardiac motion and the large-scale human gait more accurately than the 5.8GHz one. The obtained results imply the great potential to implement the 24-GHz Doppler radar system for human bio-signals detection.

articleTitle: A dual circular polarized K/Ka-band feed chain for satellite communication applications
abstract: This paper presents a dual circular polarized feed system, which comprises an enhanced multiport turnstile junction and a corrugated circular horn with high aperture efficiency. The feed system operates in the K/Ka bands with polarization diversity, achieving both right- and left-hand circular polarizations, which is particularly suitable in space reflector antennas for satellite communications applications. The feed system is designed, manufactured and measured. Measured results are in very good agreement with simulated ones. The results show that in both K- and Ka-bands, the return losses, LHCP to RHCP isolations, port isolations, and cross polarization levels are better than 25 dB, 22 dB, 58 dB, and 32dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable diplexer Using λ/2 resonator with hybrid varactor-embedded stepped-impedance open-stub and slot
abstract: In this paper, a compact reconfigurable diplexer with the wideband tuning operation and high isolation is presented. Two pairs of half-wavelength (λ/2) resonators with loaded stepped-impedance open-stubs (SIOSs) are used to allocate resonances. Meanwhile, the passband selectivity is improved due to the intrinsic transmission zero generated by SIOSs. Two pairs of varactors embedded between the resonator and SIOSs are utilized for the wideband tuning operation. To further improve the tuning configuration of passband, straight- and ring-slots under resonators and I/O ports are introduced. Based on structures mentioned above, a tunable diplexer is fabricated, which exhibits the fractional tuning range of 21.8% and 21% for dual-channel with isolation greater than 35 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Symbol detection aided minimum mean square error interference alignment
abstract: With the presence of perfect channel state information(CSI), the achievable degrees of freedom (DoF) in wireless interference networks can be linearly scaled up with the number of users. However, with the presence of imperfect CSI, the sum rate becomes degraded and full DoF may not be achievable anymore. Interference Alignment (IA) is an appealing interference management technique since it enables us to achieve significant degrees of freedom in wireless interference networks. In IA, a complex data symbol is detected via iterative calculation on precoder and combiner in reciprocal network under a same principle, such as minimum mean square error (MMSE). A symbol detection aided MMSE (SDA-MMSE) IA iterative algorithm is proposed to improve performance. It has been shown via computer simulations that the proposed detection algorithm exhibits better performance than conventional MMSE IA algorithm.

articleTitle: 3-D absorptive frequency selective reflector based on slotlines
abstract: This paper presents an absorptive frequency selective reflector (AFSR), which exhibits a flat reflection characteristic with absorption at the both sides of the reflection band. This structure formed in planar slotline structures is mainly inclusive of one lossless resonator and two lossy resonators, which are responsible for one reflection band and two absorption bands respectively. In order to minimize the coupling of these three resonators, metallic plates are utilized to make these three resonators separated. In this paper, equivalent circuit model (ECM) based on transmission line theory is introduced to describe the design concept. Then, the realization of specified structure is provided, where a good agreement of reflection coefficient results between EM simulation and ECM is achieved. The proposed AFSR features stable performance under oblique incident angles up to 40°.

articleTitle: A compact Ka-band secondary surveillance radar transceiver system
abstract: This paper presents a Ka-band secondary surveillance radar transceiver system module. Temperature compensated technique is adopted to stable the transceiver's performance. A MEMS filter and four multifunction chips based on GaAs technique are designed in this work. The transceiver system consists of these multifunction chips and MEMS filter beside with some other commercial chips. Mixers and filters are reused to reduce the system's size, which makes the system be suitable for the large-scale system integration. Furthermore, the system only has two signal terminals and one control bus to reduce the interconnection complexity. The transceiver is able to work form -55<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C to +75<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C, benefiting from the designed temperature compensation circuits on the chips. The noise figure of the receiver is less than 3.7 dB with more than 23.9 dB power gain. The maximum output power of the transmitter is larger than 30.3 dBm.

articleTitle: Preliminary results on the use of transmitarrays in 5G antenna systems
abstract: In this paper, preliminary results on the feasibility of a multibeam antenna based on the use of a transmitarray are presented. Two different configurations are considered, adopting a different type of unit-cell. Their analysis proves that TA are potentially good candidates for this application, even if an optimization of the structure could be useful to improve the antenna performances.

articleTitle: A 1T2R W-band FMCW radar system
abstract: A FMCW W-band radar system and assembly of chipset have been proposed. Low phase noise, enough transmit power and good receiver noise performance have been achieved from 81.24GHz to 85.92GHz. Range detection function has been verified through the IF output calculation. What's more, to improve the reliability of the chipset and radar system, a package for the transmitter chip has been design. Functions of the package has been verified and electromagnetic performance has been examined by simulation.

articleTitle: A low-cost broadband circularly polarized antenna with integrated feeding network
abstract: A broadband directional circularly polarized (CP) antenna is investigated by placing two pairs of parallel dipoles orthogonally in a square plane. The proposed antenna is printed on a planar structure, which integrates a sequential-phase (SP) network on a single substrate. Parasitic stepped-patches are introduced beside the two arms of each dipole to improve the axial ratio (AR) bandwidth. Measurements show that the antenna has a |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>|<;-10-dB bandwidth of 1.76-2.64 GHz (40%), a 3-dB AR bandwidth of 1.83-2.65 GHz (36.6%), and a 1-dB gain bandwidth of 1.77-2.6 GHz (38%). These three bandwidths almost cover the same frequency band. In addition, the antenna exhibits a right-hand circular polarization with a peak gain of 8.7 dBic at 2.43 GHz.

articleTitle: A low-RCS, wideband and circularly polarized metasurface antenna
abstract: This paper designs a novel circularly polarized (CP) metasurface (MS) antenna, which has the advantages of low profile, low radar cross section (RCS) and broadband operation. The MS is composed of compact polarization-dependent artificial magnetic conductors (PDAMCs). By arranging PDAMCs like a chessboard directly on the top of a circularly polarized patch antenna, the RCS can be reduced. For using a sequential-phase (SP) network and the compact structure of MS and driven patches, the antenna achieves wideband operation with high-gain performance. The simulated results indicate that the RCS at bore-sight is reduced more than 6dB from 4.87GHz to 7.34GHz and from 7.81GHz to 8.89GHz. The antenna is left-hand with the |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>|<;-10dB bandwidth from 4.79GHz to 7.3GHz, the 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth from 4.98GHz to 6.96GHz.

articleTitle: Cycle interference alignment for the full duplex communication system
abstract: This paper mainly focuses on the single-cell multiuser full-duplex system. The base station adopts the full duplex (FD) technology, and the users use the half duplex (HD) technology. The interference alignment (IA) is introduced in the system to resolve the interference between the uplink and the downlink users. Particularly, a set of cycle IA equations are designed to reach the optimal system degree of freedom (DoF). The simulation shows that the cycle IA scheme can reach the desired result.

articleTitle: Compact liquid crystal based phase shifter with integrated bias tees
abstract: Two electrically controlled tunable phase shifters based on liquid crystal (LC) material have been presented. Due to the large size and heavy weight of used external bias tees in driving circuits of LC based microwave devices, we fabricated an LC based phase shifter with integrated mini bias tees in order to broaden its potential uses. The differential phase shift up to 270°at 10 GHz was achieved in experiment under a bias voltage of 20 Vrms. For comparison, a non-integration phase shifter was also fabricated and it possesses notable performance. In the preliminary design with bias tees integrated, the mechanical layout and circuit design, as well as the soldering of the capacitors and mini bias tees were very challenging. An optimized phase shifter design with integrated mini bias tees will be shown in the near future.

articleTitle: A 10-bit 120-MS/s SAR ADC in 90nm CMOS with redundancy compensation
abstract: This paper proposes a single-channel 10-bit 120MS/s successive-approximation-register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) in 90nm CMOS process with a 1.2-V supply voltage. By using a partial-monotonic switching sequences, the common-mode voltage variation is reduced efficiently. The binary redundancy compensation technique is adopted to solve comparator errors caused by dynamic offset and DAC settling. Compared to the conventional structure, the proposed method reduces the total capacitance by 4x, which enhances the speed and decreases the chip area. The simulation results indicate that the prototype achieves a SNDR of 60.27dB and an ENOB of 9.72b with a 58.134MHz input signal at 120MHz sampling rate, while only consuming 3.24mW power.

articleTitle: Investigation of additive manufacturing methodology with mixed silver powder and SU-8 conductive ink for 3-D RF structures
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel additive manufacturing methodology to realize arbitrary 3-D RF structures. It could be briefly summarized as in-plane printing, 3-D printing and electroplating. Firstly, commercial silver powder is mixed with negative-tone photoresist SU-8 to function as a novel conductive ink for three dimensional (3-D) printing. The basic characteristics of printed traces including minimum trace width and thickness are determined by surface profile measurement results using Dektak Stylus Profiler. Subsequently, the horizontal movement of nozzle is optimized to ensure a flat surface with desired thickness. Since SU-8 is added into the conductive ink, UV irradiation and hard bake could help solidify the 3-D structures for rapid prototyping. To further improve RF performance, a layer of copper thin film is electroplated to cover surface of conductive ink. A preliminary study for validation purpose is conducted based on the configuration of non-grounded co-planar waveguide (CPW). Its measured S-parameters confirm the efficacy of proposed manufacturing methodology, which provides a promising solution and paves the way for designing 3-D RF structures.

articleTitle: A high-isolation MIMO array for FMCW radar applications
abstract: A high-isolation MIMO array for FMCW radar applications is presented in this paper. The transmit and receive elements are placed vertically in order to obtain the high-isolation between the transmit and receive antennas. A prototype of the MIMO array is fabricated and tested.

articleTitle: Characterization of an 8×8 Al microwave kinetic inductance detector array
abstract: Chinese Antarctic Kunlun Observatory is planning to construct a 5-m THz telescope (DATE5) on Dome A, Antarctica. Therefore, a THz superconducting imaging array (TeSIA) is being proposed for DATE5 to serve its scientific goals. We test an 8×8 prototype Al microwave kinetic inductance detector (MKID) array for TeSIA in a <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>He/<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>He dilution refrigerator. The resonance frequencies are designed evenly distributed in 4-5.575 GHz band with 25 MHz intervals. The responses of the MKIDs with different bath temperatures are measured and the Q factors are calculated. Detailed measurement results and analysis will be discussed.

articleTitle: Highly integrated folded reflectarray with high-resolution beam scanning ability
abstract: With the fast development of advanced millimeter-wave and terahertz (THz) technology, it brings new opportunities as well as challenges to the antenna design. Antennas It are preferred to feature low-profile, low-cost, high-gain, and easy integration with front-end circuits. A novel folded reflectarray is proposed in this paper, with a planar feeding source integrated with main reflector in a single-layered printed circuit board. The proposed antenna achieves maximum gain of 27.4 dBi at 40.25 GHz, with overall aperture size of 93 × 93 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (12.5λ×12.5λ) and height of 0.254 mm (0.034λ). Meanwhile, the beam scanning abilities with high-resolution is experimentally validated by tiling the polarizer.

articleTitle: Microstrip antenna with triple mode based on SRR structures
abstract: A novel microstrip antenna with triple modes based on split-ring resonators (SRRs) is proposed in this paper. The antenna consists of two parts: the right side adopts the dipole with the butterfly structure; two SRRs are on the left side. The antenna has three patterns: the low-frequency point has the maximum radiation direction of the +Y-direction at the far field direction; the intermediate frequency point has the omnidirectional radiation; the maximum radiation direction of the high frequency point is the — Y-direction. The field distribution, near-field reflection coefficient and far-field radiation pattern of antenna model verify the working mechanism of the antenna. The antenna has good impedance matching and potential application value in the wireless communication system.

articleTitle: An effective sparse approximate inverse preconditioner for the multi-level fast multipole algorithm
abstract: In iteratively solving the matrix equation arising from the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA), the sparse approximate inverse (SAI) preconditioner is widely employed to improve the convergence property. In this letter, based on the geometric information of nearby basis functions pairs, a new sparse pattern selecting strategy for SAI preconditioner is proposed to enhance robustness and efficiency. Compared to the conventional selecting strategies, the proposed strategy has only one variable parameter instructing the constructing time and memory usage, which is more user friendly.

articleTitle: A circular polarization transmission array antenna with low profile and high gain
abstract: A transmission array antenna with low profile and high gain operating in C-band is proposed. The antenna is composed of a feeder as source and a planar array with 14×14 unit cells as lens, both of them are working in circular polarization. The phase compensation is achieved by tuning the transmission phases of elements in the array respectively. Due to the successful conversion of wave front from quasi-spherical surface to plane, the gain of the antenna is raised to 20 dBi at 5.8 GHz and the horn antenna has a frequency band from 2.8 GHz to 8.8GHz for S11 less than -10 dB. The antenna has a good focusing performance and the profile of the transmission planar array is only 0.021 in thickness. It has a higher gain and smaller size in comparison with those of conventional one. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed antenna can not only achieve good circular polarization radiation performance, but also exhibit advantages in low profile, simple feeding structure, and low cost.

articleTitle: GaN Schottky barrier diodes for microwave power transmission
abstract: In this presentation, GaN Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs) with low access sheet resistance of 25 Ω/□ is fabricated for microwave power transmission. Turn-on voltage of about 0.43 V and ON resistance of 3.15 are achieved by introducing TiN Schottky electrode and low sheet resistance on the access layer. Breakdown voltage of 30 V and off capacitance of 7 pF are also obtained, indicating that the diode is suitable for the application in the microwave power transmission system.

articleTitle: Analysis of coplanar-to-rectangular waveguide transition at D-band for UTC-PD THz source
abstract: This letter presents a broadband coplanar-to-rectangular waveguide transition using E-plane stepped probe for unitraveling carrier photodiode (UTC-PD) THz source application. The electromagnetic wave propagates from the CPW, and then radiates from the probe into the rectangular waveguide. A window is opened in parallel with the H-plane of the WR-6 waveguide. A stepped probe connecting to the end of the coplanar waveguide (CPW) is designed to improve the impedance bandwidth. In addition, the CPW is enclosed by an aluminum box in order to prevent the electromagnetic interference. Simulated results demonstrate that the proposed transition covers the whole D band (110-170 GHz), and has a wider fractional bandwidth of 43% and lower insertion loss of 1.3 dB.

articleTitle: Large aperture size terahertz transmitarray for near-field applications
abstract: As is well known, a large-scale antenna can have constant approximate amplitude of the electric field in its near-field region. Based on this, a 140 GHz large-scale transmitarray antenna is designed, fabricated and measured in this paper for near-distance communication applications. Simulation results show that a distance of 400 mm with nearly unchanged electric field can be achieved by an antenna with an aperture size of 44×44 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (20.5 λ×20.5λ) and a distance of 3000 mm can be achieved by an antenna with an aperture size of 132×132 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (61.6λ×61.6λ). The small transmitarray antenna has a gain of 29.08 dBi, and an aperture efficiency of 19.4%. All transmitarray antennas are fabricated by the PCB technique.

articleTitle: A 100 MHz–3.2 GHz 5.1 mW area-efficient PLL clock generator
abstract: This paper introduces a low power PLL clock generator in 40 nm CMOS technology. In this work, a multi-VCO PLL with capacitance multiplication has been designed. 4 oscillators with different buffer size are employed to constitute 16 frequency bands covering a range of 1.6 GHz-3.2 GHz. Chip area is significantly reduced with the implementation of dual charge pump topology. Adaptive frequency calibration(AFC) is utilized for automatic frequency band switching. The PLL achieved a phase noise of -91.3 dBC/Hz at 1MHz offset of 3.2 GHz with a chip area of 0.045 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and power of 5.05 mW.

articleTitle: A method based on preconditioned look ahead orthogonal matching pursuit for sparse array synthesis
abstract: A sparse array synthesis approach based on look ahead orthogonal matching pursuit (LAOMP) with inter-element spacing constraints is proposed. This method can design non-uniformly spaced array with reduced number of active sensors and more accurate matching performance, an inter-element spacing constraint is enforced to ensure physically realizable solution. The numerical experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed method with comparison to standard OMP.

articleTitle: Constant-current output LCC wireless power transfer circuit
abstract: In this paper, a LCC-WPT behaving as a current source in certain condition and its optimization design method was investigated. The formula of output current has been deduced from wave base analysis, and efficiency optimization of resonance network has been designed. The analysis shows that the resonant frequency is irrespective of the load changing, and under the condition of the resonant frequency, the circuit has the characteristics of current source. At last, a 70w power rating prototype has been produced. The results have proved the constant-current feature of circuit and the 91% efficiency of prototype.

articleTitle: Chireix amplifier with enhanced bandwidth using active load
abstract: The use of an active load has been recently proposed for the realization of power-efficient broadband balanced amplifiers. The application of an active load to a dual-input Chireix amplifier is investigated in this paper for the purpose of increasing their bandwidth. An embedding device model is used to established the optimal non-Foster loads required for both the transistors to remain operating in class F as the operating frequency deviates from the center frequency. Given the transistors must operate with a constant voltage swing between backoff and peak, it is found necessary for the two transistors to operate with different load impedances as the frequency varies. The required load impedance and outphasing angles for the Chireix operation are obtained using a generalized eigenvalue problem using the Y-matrix of the Chireix combiner loaded with the active load. It is verified that using an active load, it is possible to maintain a high efficiency not only at peak power but also under various backoff power levels over a bandwidth of 1 GHz. Within a 200 MHz bandwidth, the PA is predicted to be able to maintain an efficiency larger than 79% for 6 dB backoff. Further work is required to experimentally validate the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Multimode baseband signal processing module of a digital polar transmitter for IoT applications
abstract: This paper presents a multimode baseband signal processing circuit of a digital polar transmitter for IoT applications. In order to support 802.11ah and NB-IoT standards with different signal bandwidths and wide frequency span, the asynchronous design is introduced to align different sampling clocks. Half-band filters are optimized through three aspects to reduce die area and power consumption. Moreover, digital pre-distortion technique is employed to successfully linearize the system. This chip performs frequency up-sampling, filtering operations, CORDIC, digital pre-distortion (DPD) to push image far way and improve signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

articleTitle: Implementation of MIMO antenna with wide beamwidths for Q-band short-range wireless communications
abstract: An planar integrated millimeter-wave (mmW) MIMO antenna is proposed for Q-band indoor short-range wireless communications (known as IEEE 802.11aj). The introduced MIMO antenna is comprised of four printed angled dipoles with four reflector elements, and each one has the property of wide bandwidths. Prototypes are fabricated and measured, which show that the proposed MIMO antenna has a good impedance bandwidth over 43.5~47GHz, wide bandwidths larger than 120° in their main cuts, and good isolations between any two elements. The scheme of good isolations is revealed and discussed.

articleTitle: The structure and contrast of 220GHz waveguide-to-microstrip transition
abstract: In this paper two types of waveguide-to-microstrip E-plane probe transitions are designed and analyzed by using the advanced electromagnetic simulation software HFSS in the WR4 frequency range, the center frequency is 220GHz. The first structure has been realized on 50um thick quartz substrates with S11 below -22dB and S21 below 0.88dB over the entire frequency band, and simulation results for quartz substrates of 50um and 100um thickness are compared. The second structure has been realized on 50um thick gallium arsenide substrate, S11 less than -10dB, S21 less than 1.3dB. Finally, the simulation results of the two structures are compared.

articleTitle: Accuracy improvement in range measurements of short-range FSK radars
abstract: Frequency-shift-keying (FSK) radars are used to measure the absolute range and radial speed of multiple moving targets with different velocities in short-range scenarios. The range is calculated from a well-known formula that depends on the phase difference of the in-phase/quadrature (I/Q) components associated with the two time-multiplexed transmitted tones. From a signal perspective, this work demonstrates that an additional novel term in the equation must be compensated to gain enhanced range accuracy in the measurements. This may facilitate the exploitation of longer waveform periods, leading to a relaxation in the stringent locking-time requirements currently imposed on the phase-locked loops of the signal-generation blocks in FSK radars. Moreover, detailed simulation examples for multiple moving targets are addressed. The obtained results validate the theoretical framework and the proposed computationally-efficient compensation algorithm for improved absolute-range-measurement accuracy in FSK radars.

articleTitle: A wideband rat-race coupler using stepped impedance resonator
abstract: A wideband rat-race coupler using stepped impedance resonator (SIR) has been proposed in this paper. The proposed coupler operates over frequency range of 1.70 GHz to 2.40 GHz with 35% fractional bandwidth, centered at 2.0 GHz. The measured amplitude and phase imbalances between the two out-of-phase output ports are within 0.5 dB and 180±10°. To achieve this, each branch of a conventional rat-race coupler is replaced by the SIRs. The values of the impedances of the lines are computed mathematically first and later realized using microstrip lines. The proposed design offers 75% more wider bandwidth than the conventional rat race coupler, without increasing the overall foot-print. The measured reflection co-efficient is below −10 dB with isolation better than 20 dB in the desired band. The prototype has been fabricated and measured and the results are compared with the simulated data to validate the theory.

articleTitle: A 14 × 14 electronically reconfigurable reflectarray using 1-bit reflective element
abstract: In this paper, a 14 ×14 electronically reconfigurable reflectarray for beam scanning is presented. The proposed 1-bit reflective element, which is used to construct the reflectarray, is based on PIN diodes and able to generate two reflective states with a 180° reflective phase difference and the reflection amplitudes of > -1 dB. Such two states can be switched by controlling the forward and reverse biasing of the diode. Simulated results show that scanning beams from -30° to +60° are achieved in the horizontal plane the feed located, with a peak gain of 20 dBi.

articleTitle: Dual bandpass filter based on hybrid spoof surface plasmon polariton and substrate integrated waveguide structure
abstract: A novel dual bandpass filter based on hybrid spoof surface plasmon polariton (SPP) and substrate integrated wave-guide (SIW) structure is proposed in this paper. In this design, H-shaped unite slots are etched on the top surface of SIW to form the spoof SPP. Thus, the surface wave mode of SPP can be excited and transmitted inside the closed structure of SIW. The dispersion and transmission characteristics of the proposed hybrid SIW-SPP transmission line (TL) are analyzed. Moreover, dual bandpass feature is observed in the proposed hybrid TL due to rejection introduced by capacitive-coupled series SPP.

articleTitle: A wide locking range harmonic enhanced injection locked frequency divide-by-4 with low injected power level (Invited)
abstract: In this paper, a fully differential injection which enhances the harmonics in the injection locked frequency divide-by-4 is proposed to widen the locking range with low injected power levels. Designed in Global Foundries 65nm CMOS process, the proposed injection locked frequency divide-by-4 operating at 60 GHz, achieves a locking range of 20% from 54 GHz to 66 GHz with a low injected power of -5 dBm. The proposed injection locked frequency divide-by-4 consumes 3.2 mW from a low DC supply of 0.5 V. The core area of the proposed frequency divide-by-4 is 250 μm × 230 μm.

articleTitle: Miniature dual-band bandpass filter based on E-shape dual-mode resonator
abstract: In this paper, a miniature dual-band passband filter based on open stub-loaded E-shape dual-mode resonators is proposed. The characteristics of the proposed dual-band filter are analyzed using electromagnetic simulations. The two dual-mode resonators generate four resonate modes in the first passband and two resonate modes in the second passband. An experimental filter with two passbands centred at 3.5 GHz and 7.0 GHz has been designed and fabricated. The filter response possesses two transmission zeros at 3.1 and 4.5GHz, resulting in high selectivity and stopband rejection.

articleTitle: Design of a cascaded full 360 ° reflection-type phase shifter with 90° hybrid coupler
abstract: A cascaded 360° reflection-type phase shifter with 90° hybrid coupler is presented. The phase shifter is composed with two segments and each segment adopts a hybrid coupler with reflective varactor load. The result indicates that the tunable phase range of this cascaded phase shifter is more than 360°. The insertion loss variation is less than 2dB and return loss is better than 10dB in all phase statement.

articleTitle: Extracting extremely wideband complex dielectric permittivity and effective conductivity by using one pair of SIW circular cavities
abstract: A simple and efficient method for extracting extremely wideband complex dielectric permittivity and effective conductivity is proposed and validated in this paper. Different to the conventional method which requires multiple models, suffers from narrow band applications and measurement errors, the equivalent relative dielectric constant, dielectric loss tangent and the equivalent metal conductivity can be separately extracted by using only one pair of SIW circular cavities with different height. By utilizing resonating characteristics of multiple high-order TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mno</sub> modes which are distributed within an extremely wide frequency band, the proposed method almost has no bandwidth limitation in theory. By using a printed-circuit-board (PCB) process, an experiment is used to verify the proposed method, in which all the equivalent characteristics of dielectric and metal are extracted from 8 to 60 GHz. The experiment results well verify theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: A nonplanar quad-element UWB-MIMO antenna with graphite sheet to increase the isolation
abstract: A nonplanar quad-element ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna for four-port multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) is designed in this paper. The MIMO antenna element is covered in the surface of polystyrene block with a cylindrical hole, and a thin graphite sheet which fixed with a polystyrene cylindrical block is fabricated in the column hole. This element of the antenna has a most compact size (18*20mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). The round monopole antenna elements with coplanar waveguides (CPWs)-fed are printed on the FR4. An inverted L-shaped structure with rectangle-shape slots provides the lower levels of the return loss. By the simulation, the return loss is lower 15dB over the range from 3 to 11GHz, which broadband impedance is matched. In addition, the three-dimensional (3-D) UWB-MIMO system provides high isolation between elements. Moreover, the envelope correlation coefficient is calculated, which shows good MIMO performance.

articleTitle: Study of a low-profile transmitarray element using 3 non-identical layers
abstract: The circuit model of a three-layer transmitarray element that features non-identical layers and layer spacings is presented in this paper. The matching condition and the theoretical results are discussed, and the theory shows that an element with non-identical layers can realize similar phase range as the identical-layer design but with a much lower profile. Applying this theory, a 3-layer element with unequal spacings is designed and the numerical simulation agrees well with the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Frequency-doubled phase-coded microwave signal generation based on cascaded modulators
abstract: A novel photonic approach to generate frequency-doubled phase-coded microwave signals with large frequency-tunable range is proposed. A dual-polarization modulator followed by a polarization controller is utilized to generate orthogonally polarized ±first-order optical sidebands. Then, a polarization modulator is employed to achieve the phase modulation of the two wavelengths. By beating the phase-modulated orthogonally polarized ±first-order optical sidebands in a balanced photodetector, a frequency-doubled phase-coded microwave signal is generated. The proposed phase-coded microwave signal generator features compact structure, high stability, and most importantly, ultra-wide operating bandwidth. By applying different coding signals, the proposed approach can also generate arbitrarily modulated signals.

articleTitle: A reflectarray using log-periodic dipole array element
abstract: This paper presents a study of reflectarray using a log-periodic dipole array (LPDA) element. Wideband scattering performance of the LPDA element is demonstrated numerically. A five elements linear reflectarray is designed and fabricated. Scattering performance of the fabricated reflectarray was measured in order to show its wideband scattering performance experimentally.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a multi-channel frequency synthesizer for 5G wireless communication systems
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a multi-channel frequency synthesizer for 5G massive MIMO systems of 3.4-3.6 GHz. This frequency synthesizer is based on a microwave wideband synthesizer chip with integrated VCO. Several considerations for balancing the performance of phase noise, spurs, frequency resolution and locking time are discussed. The proper phase detector frequency, loop filter, RF and power filtering circuit are designed. To apply this frequency synthesizer to 64-channel massive MIMO systems with local frequency of 3.875 GHz, an 8-way Wilkinson power splitter with amplifier modules is also designed. According to this structure, the frequency synthesizer with excellent performance is developed. The experimental results indicate that the output of frequency synthesizer is with low phase noise (<;106 dBc/Hz@10KHz) and low spurious (<;-83 dBc) at 3.875 GHz for multi-channel. Besides, it can achieve wideband with a very fine resolution without residual frequency error, which make it possible to be used in other systems.

articleTitle: Dual-chirp microwave waveform generation for radar application based on an optically injected semiconductor laser
abstract: A photonic-based dual-chirp linear frequency modulated (LFM) microwave waveform generator is proposed based on an optically injected semiconductor laser. A dual-chirp LFM waveform can be used in a radar system to improve its range-Doppler resolution. A proof of experiment is taken. A dual-chirp LFM signal with frequency range of 13.4-20.5 GHz and a time duration of 2 μs is realized.

articleTitle: Study of terahertz MIMO imaging with fast reconstruction algorithm
abstract: In this paper, a design of MIMO array for 0.2 THz imaging was studied. An imaging algorithm with high efficiency was developed by successfully implementing the phase shift migration (PSM) into MIMO reconstruction. To numerically verify the imaging quality and the proposed method, the scattered data of targets was obtained based on the near-field distribution of the transceiving antenna from full wave electromagnetic simulations. With the multistatic scattered data rearranged in spatial frequency domain, image with high quality was reconstructed based on MIMO-PSM algorithm, with greatly improved efficiency as compared to the conventional back-projection (BP) algorithm. The work in this paper provides a guideline for THz-MIMO array design and proposed a fast imaging algorithm for MIMO imaging.

articleTitle: A compact passive resonator based on through-silicon via technology for microwave applications
abstract: Based on the TSV technology, a compact passive resonator utilizing spiral inductor and coaxial TSV capacitor is proposed. And the compact stack configuration integrates the whole resonator in a microsize as small as 75μm×75μm. Furthermore, the adopted spiral inductor, coaxial TSV capacitor and resonator are characterized with equivalent circuit model. The transmission parameters from equivalent circuit models and HFSS simulation are matched very well. The proposed resonator exhibits an insertion loss below 1.0dB and a return loss over -20 dB at the center frequency of 2.7GHz in the passband. And the -3dB bandwidth of resonant peak in the resonant frequency span are within the range from 1.4GHz to 5.2GHz, which demonstrates the superior characteristic of the resonator.

articleTitle: Design of slot-coupled diamond-shape microstrip wideband bandpass filter
abstract: A slot-coupled diamond-shape wideband bandpass filter is proposed in this paper. It consists of diamond-shape microstrip lines in the top and bottom layers coupled through a diamond-shape slot in the middle layer. It is analyzed by conformal mapping theory. Two interdigital coupled lines are used to improve out-of-band performance. Simulation result using HFSS shows the proposed filter has a wideband response with 3dB bandwidth from 2.55 to 7.05GHz (93.75%) and flat group delay of 0.32ns.

articleTitle: A simple method to generate orbital angular momentum beams with microstrip ring antenna
abstract: In this paper, a simple method to generate orbital angular momentum beams is proposed in microwave regime. The fundamental TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode and the higher order TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub>, TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</sub>, TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">41</sub> modes of an annular micrstrip ring are adopted to generate different OAM states. All the modes are fed by the same signals, where two ports with equal amplitude and 90° phase difference are used. The angle between the two feeding locations is reduced as the mode order increases. The simulation results verify the feasibility of this method. The TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>, TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub>, TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</sub>, and TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">41</sub> modes of the ring are responsible for the ±1, ±2, ±3, ±4 OAM states, respectively.

articleTitle: Compact balanced filters with enhanced differential-mode out-of-band response using coupled slotline structure
abstract: Two compact balanced filters using coupled slotline structure are presented in this paper with intrinsic common-mode (CM) rejection and enhanced differential-mode (DM) out-of-band response. By properly designing the proposed U2 folded stepped-impedance slotline resonators (SISRs), compact size and extended DM upper-stopband rejection could be achieved. Specifically, two balanced filters with second-order and third-order coupled slotline resonators (SRs) are implemented. Measured and simulated results are in approximate agreement with each other, showing inherent CM rejection and enhanced DM out-of-band performance such as improved selectivity, multiple transmission zeros (TZs) as well as extended upper stopband.

articleTitle: Equivalent 2-port of cascade WPT systems
abstract: This paper presents a simple method to transform cascade wireless power transfer (WPT) systems consisting of transmitter, receiver and multiple repeater antennas to equivalent two-port network using matrix reduction technique. The method is first derived in a conventional 3-coil system. S parameter simulation is performed in ANSYS HFSS for validation. The proposed method provides a convenient way to analyze complex cascade WPT systems under the scope of two-port network and can be applied in systems with arbitrary number of repeaters.

articleTitle: A compressed sensing method for pruning concurrent dual-band power amplifier models
abstract: This paper presents a compressed sensing (CS) method for pruning concurrent dual-band power amplifier (PA) behavioral models. The method is based on the sparsity assumption for kernel and coefficients of a dual-band PA model. The orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm is adopted as a substitution of the traditional least square method to extract the model coefficients. Experimental results show that the similar model accuracy and DPD performance can be achieved by the proposed method, while the model complexity is lower because the number of the kernel and coefficients is reduced.

articleTitle: Substrate integrated waveguide technology applied to dynamic beam forming techniques for 5G applications: Challenges and opportunities
abstract: This contribution presents the challenges and opportunities related to the employment of Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) structures in mm-W 5G array systems with beam forming properties. These architectures usually include arrays of more than 100 antenna elements organized in sub-clusters, which are fed with proper amplitude and phase in order to obtain beam-steering capabilities. These systems generally operate in Ka band, on bandwidths that are larger than 10%, which calls for antennas that are capable of covering large frequency spans with uniform performance. The use of Substrate Integrated Waveguide technology in the design of both the antenna elements and the feeding section can help introduce features that reduce the system complexity, enhance antenna isolation, and allow for a low-cost implementation. Moreover, the use of tunable SIW antenna elements can introduce reconfigurability properties in clustered array configurations, opening for a number of advantages in terms of dynamic performance enhancement.

articleTitle: A 1GSps RF sampling pipelined ADC with novel background digital calibration
abstract: This paper presents a novel high accuracy background calibration design for pipelined ADC. Pseudorandom (PN) sequences are used for gain error calibration but also limit the calibration accuracy because of the inherent quantization noise. So we add redundant stages and derive new algorithm to reduce the impact of quantization noise and improve the accuracy of gain error calibration. A 12-Bit 1Gsps RF sampling pipelined ADC using our proposed digital calibration has been designed. Both behavioral and post simulation indicates the proposed calibration works effectively, where the post simulation results show the ADC reaches an SNDR of 66.6 dB (ENOB=9.72-Bit) at 1GSps sampling rate after the calibration.

articleTitle: Notice of Removal: Extended stopband balanced filter with asymmetrical coupled lines
abstract: Removed.

articleTitle: Efficient algorithms for moving objects localization and tracking based on continuous Wave Doppler radar
abstract: Continuous-wave Doppler radar has been proposed for decades and widely used both in military detection and for civil use, to capture or recognize the motion of objects. Conventionally, continuous-wave Doppler radar is vulnerable in locating the absolute trajectory of the object. In this paper, we use I/Q modulation to receive the echo of hand. A real-time adaptive algorithm is proposed to determine the center of a series of phasor constellation. We also preset three antennas in a line to receive the echo containing Doppler information. Thus, a numerical solution of the trajectory of single object has been proposed, which makes it possible to track objects via continuous wave Doppler radar.

articleTitle: A generalized nonlinear detector for impulse radio UWB receiver employed square law technology
abstract: In this paper, a generalized nonlinear detector (GND) is proposed for impulse radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB) receiver employed the nonlinear square law (SL) technology (SL-GND). By using a generalized nonlinear detector, the received signal processed by SL operator is exploited by it's high-order statistic. Simulation results show that comparing with the conventional ED receivers using SL technology and other nonlinear detector-based receiver, the proposed SL-GND receiver can significantly improve the bit-error-rate performance, especially when strong narrowband interference presents.

articleTitle: Wideband architecture for passive intermodulation localization
abstract: Passive intermodulation is caused by electromagnetic nonlinearity of passive devices, and it can seriously interfere with the quality of wireless communication. The high-accuracy of passive intermodulation measure and localization is significance in PIM research and related architecture of wireless communication system. In this paper, we construct a wideband localization system of passive intermodulation based on carrier suppression. Instead of selecting high selectivity for BPF to extract weak PIM product, we used carrier suppression to cancel strong reflect two-tone signal and then measure the PIM product. This localization system can work between 0.7GHz∼2.3GHz. Simulation analysis, carrier suppression system can realize 70dB attenuation of test signals. This method can be widely used in the checking, testing of high power microwave systems.

articleTitle: Single-ended-to-balanced balun-based dual-band power divider with open-ended stubs
abstract: A balun-based five-port dual-band power divider with single-ended input and two differential-ended outputs is proposed. Its dual operational ranges extend from 1.3 GHz to 2.22 GHz with a center frequency of 1.77 GHz for the first band and from 3.12 GHz to 3.8 GHz with a center frequency of 3.5 GHz for the second band. This dual-band behavior is attained by means of the use of open-ended stubs in the power-divider topology. A proof-of-concept prototype of this single-ended-to-balanced power divider is developed and tested with close agreement between measurements and simulations. A proper dual-band power-division functionality for the single-to-differential-mode operation is achieved. Moreover, at the measured dual operational frequencies, the suppression of the common-mode noise is less than 28 dB and the mode-conversion mitigation between differential-mode signals and common-mode noise is below 32 dB.

articleTitle: Compact LTCC balun filter with high level harmonic suppression using discriminating coupling
abstract: This paper presents a compact low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) balun filter with the second harmonic suppression. It is composed of two half-wavelength resonators and three feeding lines. The 180° phase difference between two output ports is obtained owing to the out-of-phase characteristic at the two open ends of the half-wavelength resonator. By using discriminating coupling between feeding lines and resonators, the second harmonic is rejected. The coupling coefficient in the passband can be tuned to the desired value through the gap. A LTCC balun filter centered at 4.6 GHz is implemented. Good agreement between the simulated and measured results is observed. The stopband rejection below 34 dB is from 1.2f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> to 2.6f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> and the core circuit size is 3.3 mm × 2.7 mm × 1.6 mm or 0.122λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub> × 0.1λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub>× 0.059λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub>.

articleTitle: A compact quad-band bandpass filter with high skirt selectivity based on stub-loaded resonators and λ/4 resonators
abstract: In this paper, a quad-band bandpass filter (BPF) with compact size and high skirt selectivity is proposed by using j both stub-loaded resonators (SLRs) and λ/4 resonators. One set of SLRs is utilized not only to generate the lower passbands but also to feed the λ/4 resonators. Three extra transmission zeros (TZs) are created in the stopband by using a zero feed structure. For demonstration, a exemplary filter has been designed and fabricated. Good agreement is observed between the simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: Compact 28-GHz two-dimensionally scanning multibeam array with sidelobe suppression
abstract: This work presents a compact 28-GHz two-dimensionally (2-D) scanning multibeam array antenna with sidelobe suppression in substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology. The proposed antenna is comprised of a 2 × 8 slot array and a beam-forming network (BFN), which is realized by combining two dual-layer 4 × 8 Butler matrixes (BMs) and four 90° couplers. The introduced 4 × 8 BM can help suppress the sidelobe level (SLL) in the E-plane so that the anti-interference capability in the E-plane can be improved. Taking the complicated structure of the classic 4 × 8 BM into account, some modifications of the BM are conducted to achieve better compactness.

articleTitle: A broadband CMOS amplifier in D band using pole-tuning technique with T-type network
abstract: A novel pole-tuning technique with T-type network for interstage bandwidth extension is proposed in this paper. For verification, a four-stage amplifier based on the pole-tuning technique with T-type network has been designed and implemented in a 65-nm bulk CMOS technology. The fabricated prototype achieves a peak gain of 9.5 dB at 122 GHz with a 3-dB bandwidth of 26 GHz, while consuming a dc power of 62 mW. The saturation output power and the output P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</sub> are 8.6 dBm and 4.6 dBm, respectively. The chip occupies a small silicon area of 0.27 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including all testing pads.

articleTitle: TR-OFDM-MIMO platform developed for intra-spacecraft wireless communications
abstract: A software defined radio based time reversal orthogonal frequency division multiplexing multiple-input multiple-output (TR-OFDM-MIMO) platform has been developed at University of Electronic Science and Technology of China (UESTC) for the purpose of intra-spacecraft wireless communication applications. After describing the principle and basic architecture of the TR-OFDM-MIMO platform, an experimental demonstration of wireless video transmission in a closed metal box is presented. The results show that the developed platform works reliably inside the richly scattering metal box, indicating a promising solution to the mission of cable-free data transfer inside the closed space capsules.

articleTitle: Wideband balun filter on multi-mode resonator with good performance in magnitude and phase
abstract: A novel wideband balun filter on multi-mode slotline resonator topology with good balanced performance in magnitude and phase is reported in this paper. The proposed wideband balun filter consists of one uniform half-wavelength slot-line resonator (SLR), one single-ended unbalanced port, and one balanced port with two terminals. By utilizing the distinct field conversion from the slotline to the microstrip feeding line, the proposed balun filter can realize good balanced performance in magnitude and phase over a wideband frequency range. In order to demonstrate the proposed scheme and support the design conception, one wideband balun filter prototype is designed, fabricated, and tested. All of the measured results of frequency response, magnitude and phase imbalance performance agree well with the simulated one, and have effectively demonstrated the good frequency selectivity and balanced performance in both magnitude and phase over a wide frequency band.

articleTitle: High resolution TDC and high linearity DTC for all-digital spur calibration
abstract: This paper presents an all-digital spur calibration method based on a high resolution time-to-digital converter (TDC) and high linearity digital-to-time converters (DTC). The proposed TDC achieves high resolution with small area while the high linearity DTCs reduce the calibration time. The timing errors are measured with a Vernier TDC which can amplify the errors to improve the time resolution. The errors will be corrected by DTCs later. By using the proposed TDC, the resolution achieves 200 fs with a total conversion range of ±4.2 ps. The proposed DTCs are based on constant slope charging method driven by two digital-to-analog converters (dAC). Rising and falling edge delay can be controlled independently. With 8-bit DACs and 9 ps linear range for each edge, the maxim integral nonlinearity (iNl) is 41.6 fs. After calibration, time error of each multi-phase signal will be reduced to less than 120 fs on average.

articleTitle: General G-matrix imaging method for near-field millimeter-wave SAIR with any arrays
abstract: For utilizing array antennas effectively, various array configurations are used in millimeter-wave synthetic aperture imaging radiometer (SAIR). However, existing imaging methods are usually adapted to specific arrays, can't be used to compare the imaging performance of SAIRs with different arrays. To overcome this shortage, a General G-matrix Imaging Method (GGIM) is proposed in this paper. For reconstructing the millimeter-wave images accurately, the General G-matrix model with high accuracy is established according to near-field synthetic aperture imaging principle firstly. Then the reconstruction is performed by solving the underdetermined G-matrix equation. Compared to other imaging methods, the proposed GGIM can be used in arbitrary SAIRs, and its inversion accuracy is higher than the traditional imaging methods.

articleTitle: Progressive LO phase shifting technique with linear coupled oscillators in 90nm BiCMOS
abstract: A linear coupled oscillator based LO phase shifting system is integrated in 90nm BiCMOS technology. A two element coupled oscillator network and a frequency quadrupler are designed for x4 phase shifting range. The LO chain is proposed for 71-76GHz beamforming transceiver. With injection locking technique, the phase noise of -122dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset is measured. 300MHz locking range is achieved with +5dBm injection power. The measured maximum phase progression is +/-80 degree. The power consumption of PALNA in Tx/Rx mode is 86.5/30 mW and each LO path consumes 60mW.

articleTitle: Design of a high linearity power amplifier in GaN HEMT technology
abstract: A 37.5dBm high-linearity power amplifier working in Ku band is presented. This power amplifier is fabricated in a 0.25μm gate process with GaN high electron mobility transistor. To improve the linearity characterization, two circuits were designed with different output matching network. The first one is matched to the optimum load for PAE characterization while the second is matched to the optimum load for linearity characterization which is quantized by IM3. Measured results indicate that the largest output power is up to 37.5dBm and the best PAE can get up to 36%. Measured linearity results of the two circuits are also presented. PAE of the second circuit is 2~4 lower than first one while linearity is 1~2dBc up than the first one. The results show that output matching network can be matched close to the optimum load for linearity characterization in order to get higher linearity.

articleTitle: A method of VSIE for electromagnetic scattering by planar composite conductor-dielectric structures
abstract: A method of moments (MoM) based on volume-surface integral equation (VSIE) for analyzing electromagnetic scattering of planar composite conductor-dielectric structures is studied. In the dielectric, the prism basis function is used for the tangential electric field and the pulse basis function is used for the normal electrical field to expand the electric flux density in both directions. The conductor surface current is expanded with Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) basis function. In the process of discrete integral equations, the calculation of impedance matrix elements can be implemented through the calculation of impedance matrix elements in the surface integral equation due to the planar characteristics of the structure. Numerical results verify the accuracy of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: On optimization of miller divider with transformer injection enhancement
abstract: In this paper, we present an optimization technique to get maximum locking range for Miller frequency divider topology with transformer injection enhancement. The injection locking portrait has been employed to optimize such Miller divider topologies. The proposed Miller divider has been designed in a standard 40 nm mm-Wave CMOS process for which the models are valid up to 100 GHz. Post layout simulation results show that the optimized divider can operate over the total operating range of 30 GHz (44.5 GHz-74.5 GHz) for 0 dBm input injection power at a center frequency of 59.5 GHz with power dissipation of 5.5 mW, showing better Bandwidth vs Input injection power ratio than unoptimized divider.

articleTitle: Metasurface for high isolation in MIMO antenna
abstract: A strip structure metasurface operating at 2-14GHz is designed for high isolation of 2-element MIMO antenna. The strip structure is a single layer rectangular patch with some square slits. The strip structure metasurface has over 5.3GHz for S21<;-30dB in operating band. Then the strip structure metasurface is extended to the cross structure metasurface, which has the same operating band and can be used for 4-element MIMO antenna. The cross structure metasurface has over 6GHz for S21<;-30dB, 1.8GHz for S31<;-30dB, 3.3GHz for S41<;-30dB and 4.6GHz for S42<;-30dB in operating band. A microstrip MIMO antenna is used to verify the improvement.

articleTitle: Power maximization for capacitive wireless power transfer with two transmitters and one receiver
abstract: Inductive wireless power transfer from multiple transmitters to a single receiver has already been studied. However, for capacitive power transfer, an analysis of a multi transmitter setup has not yet been performed, even though useful applications are being developed for this technology. In this work, we determine the optimal solution for a capacitive wireless power transfer system in order to maximize the power transfer from two transmitter sources to a single load at the receiver side. As well the case for uncoupled as coupled transmitters is solved. We find that for the uncoupled configuration, a purely resistive load optimizes the system, whereas for the coupled configuration, a susceptance has to be inserted to maximize the power transfer. We confirm our results by circuit simulations.

articleTitle: Accurate metrology of freestanding wire polarizer characterization for terahertz sounding
abstract: The configuration, fabrication and determination of freestanding wire polarizer (FWP) were demonstrated for lower end of THz. Tungsten wire with a diameter of 10-micron was selected to ensure excellent propagation and reflectance up to 500GHz. It can be assumed that this FWP could keep approximated performance up to about 700GHz. The measurement results were in good agreement with the theoretical results by adopting Gaussian quasi-optic measurement system.

articleTitle: A compact six-order folded-waveguide resonator filter
abstract: A new compact 6-order bandpass filter design based on a folded waveguide (FWG) resonator structure is presented. The ridge waveguide is an important transmission line for broadband communication systems. This reduces the size of the filter. Then fold this filter along the center coordinates. It has no coupling or tuning screws. A full-wave simulator has been employed for designing the filter. The filter expands the 3dB fractional bandwidth to 8.2% at the center frequency of 3.5 GHz. This filter also provides an improved selectivity characteristic with compact size compared with the conventional resonator filters.

articleTitle: Triangle SIW planar slot antenna with improved gain
abstract: In this paper, a novel, low-profile cavity backed 2×1-slot antenna utilizing the substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) technology is proposed. The antenna includes a thin equilateral triangle substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity with a single radiating slot at upper edge. In the feeding layer, a SIW operating in the fundamental mode TE110 is accommodated. The performance is numerically evaluated by means of the method of finite elements. Measurement results indicate that using 2×1-slot backed by a triangle SIW cavity, it can improve antenna gain by 1.8dB over the gain of the single-slot antenna at the cost of a slight increase of the dimensions, which shows that this antenna retains good radiation performance of conventional cavity backed antennas.

articleTitle: Bandpass-to-all-pass reconfigurable filter with wide frequency tuning range
abstract: In this work, we propose and demonstrate a bandpass-to-all-pass reconfigurable filter with a wide frequency tuning range. The proposed filter employs frequency-tunable substrate integrated resonators and transmission line with two single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switches. The frequency-tunable second-order reconfigurable filter is designed to support the presented design theory and both operating modes are well obtained.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of back-to-back horn array with rippled patterns
abstract: A back-to-back horn antenna is presented and analyzed in this paper. The antenna features rippled beams and omnidirectional radiation to evaluate an advanced millimeter-wave (mmWave) measurement setup for probe-fed antennas. Substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technique is used in antenna design. Based on the vector superposition principle, an approximate formula is derived to determine the form of rippled beam, and is then validated by full-wave simulation.

articleTitle: High gain and low flicker noise down-conversion mixer applied in 24GHz FMCW radar
abstract: Millimeter-wave radar for speed and range measurement becomes a certain with the need of autonomous vehicles. In recent years, there are more research in 24GHz FMCW radar, while the low-noise and high gain down-conversion mixer is still a difficulty to solve. This article presents a folded Gilbert cell active mixer realized in SMIC55nm process. The conversion gain is 17.1dB, and NF is 9.2dB. S11 is -33.8dB in 24GHz, and power is 4.4mW. This design achieves the goal of high gain and low NF at same time with low power.

articleTitle: Design of high efficiency single-layered transparent metasurface and its application for circularly polarized lens antenna
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-thin single-layered transparent metasurface (MS) is proposed to focus circularly polarized (CP) waves in transparent geometry with high efficiency. A single-layered phasing element is firstly optimized to meet the demands of Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) phase theory. Firstly, a one dimensional phase gradient MS is devised with phase difference of 60°between adjacent cells, in order to validate the surface capability of manipulating transmitted waves. Secondly, a novel planar focusing metasurface (PFM) is designed with focal length of 40mm and size of 102×102mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> as well as cells of 15×15. The pretty good focusing effect of the CP metasurface lens contributes to its application for high gain lens antenna. Finally, by placing a CP patch antenna at the focal spot of the PFM as the feed source, the excellent performances of the MS lens antenna are obtained in terms of realized gain of 20.7 dB, aperture efficiency of 41.3%, half power beam width (HPBW) of 14° near 14GHz.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable sensing antenna for mechanical rotation monitoring
abstract: A UHF-band reconfigurable sensing antenna (RSA) based on passive RFID technology is presented in this paper. In order to monitor mechanical rotations, a rotatable elliptical patch antenna is proposed. The rotatable patch is fed by a fixed slot, on which a RFID chip is integrated. This elliptical patch could rotate a specific angle driven by a sensing component such as a thermal bi-metal coil, and the resonant frequency changes accordingly. To increase the read range of the RSA, a back cavity is added on the other side of the slot. The cavity enhances the gain to 4.74dB, which results in a 20m read range in simulation.

articleTitle: A compact UWB-RFID sensor tag with reconfigurable band-notch deployment
abstract: In UWB-RFID sensor system, the interference from other wireless protocol with the frequency overlapped each other is becoming a main issue to determine the accuracy of sensitivity in terms of a specific identification. One solution to tackle the problem is to etch a U-slot on antenna facet that can render a tag with band-notch in a specific frequency, and the band-notch can be further reconfigured by adding a PIN diode on the U-slot set by a DC bias. However, when increasing the compactness of the tag further while decreasing the EM interference brought by the added circuitry of DC bias as much as possible, a revised solution is proposed in this paper. The U-slot is placed on the grounding plane, not on the antenna facet anymore. Simulation has verified that the revised solution can be able to form the same band-notch in a given frequency band segment, and the circuitry routine used for delivering DC bias could be naturally constructed by the networking serially formed by the proposed micro-strip feed line, the substrate, the via hole, the PIN diode and the grounding plane.

articleTitle: High efficient and high reliable GaN RF device for 5G communication
abstract: GaN RF device is considered as an advanced solution for 5G development. In this paper, novel designs and processing technologies are introduced to enhance the device performance, and high efficient and reliable RF GaN Devices are characterized.

articleTitle: Design of a Q-band six-way spatial power combining structure
abstract: In this paper, a high-efficiency six-way spatial power combiner structure is presented. The structure is composed of a three-way branch-waveguide coupler with phase compensation and a waveguide T-junction with all ports matching and isolation between output ports. As a sample, a back-to-back six-way waveguide prototype, operating at 45 GHz is designed, fabricated and measured. The measurement results show that the insertion loss of the power combiner is less than 0.75 dB over the frequency range of 42-48 GHz, which demonstrates the low-loss performance of the proposed power combiner.

articleTitle: A general method for extending a lossy network to a lossless network using the matrix decomposition
abstract: In the paper, we discuss a method to extend an arbitrary reciprocal lossy network, which may be a passive device or a passive network cascaded by a series of passive devices, to a reciprocal lossless matrix. Meanwhile, we analytically proved that the scattering matrix of the extended lossless network has the smallest order, in another word, this method can calculate the least essential ports to be extended. Hence, the method build a bridge between the lossy network and the lossless network. Furthermore, the desired lossy network can be extracted from the well-designed lossless network which can be synthesized based on mature lossless methods.

articleTitle: Analytical I-V model of TID-effect in NMOSFET at low gate voltages
abstract: In this paper, an analytical model suitable for circuit simulation is presented to evaluate the TID radiation effect on n-MOSFET leakage current with LOCOS isolation under low gate voltages. In order to avoid the complexity that divides dielectric region into large number of segments when calculating the charge and drain current inherent in numerical method, an equivalent charges and interface traps in gate oxide, and backward use of mid-gap separation method are proposed to simulate the device drain current under radiation. Simulation results of the model agree well with experimental data.

articleTitle: Wide-angle SAR imaging based on sub-apertures joint sparse reconstruction
abstract: By synthesizing the sub-aperture images at various aspect angles, wide-angle synthetic aperture radar (SAR) can produce a reflectivity estimate for each spatial location and some information on anisotropy, which is useful for scene interpretation and target recognition. In order to improve the imaging resolution and decrease the sampled data, compressed sensing (CS) can be applied to each sub-aperture image formation independently. However, the independent processing is easily affected by the registration errors and the anisotropic scattering behavior of the target, resulting in many desultory points existed in the synthesis image. In this paper, a joint sparse reconstruction method of sub-aperture images is proposed, efficiently solving the above problem. By exploiting the correlation among subaperture images, defining the mixed norm with comprehensive information of full aperture, and constructing the joint sparse reconstruction model of sub-aperture images constricted by the mixed norm, the method can realize the precise match and suppress desultory points in the synthesis image. At last, the experimental data processing results verify the effectiveness and validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of a 5.9GHz ultra-low power sub-harmonic mixer for Internet of vehicles applications
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-low power down-conversion sub-harmonic mixer for Internet of vehicles (IoV) applications. The proposed mixer adopts a frequency doubler based topology to maximize the second harmonic of local oscillation (LO) signal for the frequency down conversion. The dedicated design was implemented in a 0.13-μm CMOS technology and exhibits a conversion gain of 10.3 dB at 5.9 GHz with a 0 dBm LO power level at 2.9 GHz. The core circuit of the proposed sub-harmonic mixer consumes only 187 uA current from a 1.5 V voltage supply. The mixer has a core area of 0.36 × 0.4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A broadband Doherty power amplifier based on rotated T-shape load modulation network
abstract: In this paper, a rotated T-shape load modulation network (RTLMN) is presented to extend the bandwidth at output power back-off (OBO) of a Doherty power amplifier (DPA). Theoretical analysis reveals that wider bandwidth in back-off region can be achieved by the proposed power combination network compared to the quarter wavelength transmission line (QWTL). A broadband 13-Watt DPA using two different GaN HEMTs as asymmetric cells was implemented to verily the proposed network. Measurement results show that the drain efficiency (DE) range from 52.2%-67.4% at 6-dB OBO and 66.4%-82.4% at saturation power from 2.1 GHz to 2.6 GHz.

articleTitle: A high directivity fabry-perot antenna based on metamaterial substrate
abstract: A Fabry-Perot resonator (FPR) antenna with metamaterial substrate which is fed by air-coupled patch antenna is presented in this paper. The FPR resonator consists of a partially reflective surface (PRS) formed by one metamaterial substrate, two layers offrequency selective surface (FSS) and metal ground plane. This three layers of substrate stuck together as PRS is constructed to lower the profile of the resonator antenna and enhance the directive performance. The influence of a left-handed metamaterial (LHM) substrate attached to the FSS is illustrated. From the results obtained, it is noted that in the presence of the LHM substrate, the Fabry-Perot resonator antenna becomes more directive, and has a gain enhancement by 8.4dB at 14GHz.

articleTitle: New LU decomposition accelerating parallel method of moments and its application
abstract: A novel method of panel factorization algorithm named No Pivoting in the part of LU decomposition (NPLU) is introduced based on strictly diagonally dominant property of matrix produced by parallel Method of Moments (MoM), the most importance is that this novel method eliminates the MPI communication of pivoting process entirely and accelerates LU decomposition process which is most time-consuming. The efficiency solving matrix using this algorithm compares with the most important math libraries: commercial Math Kernel Li-brary(MKL) and thus accelerates the process of LU decomposition. The results show that using the novel LU decomposition algorithm proposed in this paper not only can solve electromagnetic problems accurately, but also can accelerate the process of solving matrices.

articleTitle: Feed-forward equalizer for high speed serial electrical communication up to 100 Gb/s
abstract: This paper presents the design, trade-offs, practical limits and system-level simulations of a very high bandwidth feed-forward equalizer for high-speed serial electrical communication up to 100 Gb/s. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first detailed evaluation of an 100 Gb/s chip-to-chip interconnection based on a fully functional transistor-level circuit design and measured PCB interconnections. This approach provides the most accurate simulation model for such high transmission rates, for which many effects need to be modelled.
