The feed-forward equalizer based on a transversal filter topology is added to the transmitter signal path in order to compensate the losses over copper transmission line traces up to 50 GHz and to generate a high speed data path which is applied to transmit data up to 100 Gb/s by using partial response signaling over 5 cm to 15 cm striplines. The 5-tap symbol spaced feed-forward equalizer is designed in a 0.13 um SiGe BiCMOS technology, with an active area of 3.5 mm <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and a power consumption of around 213 mW from a 2.5 V power supply.

articleTitle: Performance comparison of divide-by-2 injection-locked frequency divider with balanced and unbalanced injection methods
abstract: This letter reports measured locking range of a CMOS divide-by-2 injection-locked frequency divider (ILFD) using two direct injection MOSFETs. The fabricated 0.18 μm CMOS +2 ILFD uses direct cross-coupled switching transistors and a RLC resonator, and it has two oscillation frequency bands. Two injection methods: balanced and unbalanced configurations are applied to analyze the circuit performance. In the balanced case, the ILFD has a single-band like locking range. In the unbalanced, three locking ranges can be identified. The consumed power of the +2 ILFD core is 10 mW at the dc drain-source voltage 0.8 V. At an external injected signal power Pinj = 0 dBm, the measured locking range is 5.7 GHz from 4.0 to 9.7 GHz.

articleTitle: Predicting influence of the rest spherical surface on the instantaneous parabolic surface of multi-beam for radio astronomy
abstract: The instantaneous parabolic antenna deformed from an active spherical main reflector in real time has been proposed for years to achieve space scanning without rotating the giant body of radio telescope and enable the realization of wide bandwidth, high sensitivity, full polarization capability and multiple beams by standard feed design. When the reflector is operating in a wide bandwidth, the inevitable energy leaking into the rest spherical surface will influence the illuminated parabolic surface. When the feed moves along the focus plane to track the radio source, the influence varies with the changing leakage energy. In order to predict this influence, a dual-polarization, 19-beam feed with relative bandwidth of 32% is designed and the calculation principles of the influence is derived, and simulated results of the independent illuminated parabolic reflector and the hybrid reflector are compared with each other to evaluate the influence.

articleTitle: Design and optimization of high shape factor high-order substrate integrated waveguide filter with cross coupling
abstract: In this paper, one kind of design and optimization method for high shape factor substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filter is presented. This design process gives a fast and accurate solution process for high frequency complex SIW filters. And the implement of a 5-order SIW bandpass filter (BPF) based on cross-coupling technology by using this optimization method has been investigated and experimentally examined in detail. The measured results are in good agreement with simulation result and verify the performance of this design and optimization method.

articleTitle: Tunable terahertz absorber using double-layer decussate graphene ribbon arrays
abstract: A tunable graphene-based terahertz perfect absorber consists of periodic double-layer decussate graphene ribbons is proposed. In the proposed absorber, the two arrays of graphene ribbons are separated by the dielectric zro2. From the bottom up, the multi-layer absorber structure is made up of Au/ zro2/graphene materials respectively. The reflection of all the electromagnetic waves is effectively restricted in the interlayer between the graphene ribbons and the metal plate, and the transmission of electromagnetic waves is also suppressed due to thick metal base. By varying the chemical potential graphene, the peak absorption frequency can be flexibly tuned. By changing the geometric parameters of the structure, more than 99% absorbance can be achieved. Moreover, the graphene absorber has a simple structure and can be easily manufactured by an existing manufacturing process, such absorber will benefit the fabrication of detecting, sensing and optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: A novel stacked class-E-like power amplifier with dual drain output power technique in 0.18 um RFSOI CMOS technology
abstract: A novel stacked class-E-like power amplifier (PA) topology with dual drain output power technique is proposed in this paper. Owing to the dual drain output power enhanced technique, the total output power is 1.25 times of the conventional class-E PA with single drain output. Meanwhile, benefited from the low ON resistance switch device on high resistance and trap-rich substrate of RFSOI technology, high PAE and low cost performance are also obtained. In particular, a differential dual drain output power class-E-like PA with an on-chip transformer based power combiner has been implemented in 0.18 um radio frequency silicon-on-insulator CMOS (RF SOI CMOS) technology. Experimental results show a peak PAE of 51% for the class-E-like PA with saturated output power of 29.6 dBm at 1.8 GHz 2.5 V supply voltage.

articleTitle: Root-locus method for the stability analysis of high-order FDTD
abstract: In this article, the Root-Locus method is used for the stability analysis of the high-order staggered finite difference time domain implementation of Two-Pole Debye dispersive media. It is shown that the position of the wave-equation roots in the complex plane determines whether the stability of the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method and allows the computation of the Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL). Numerical simulations are carried out for Two-Pole Debye model to validate the obtained results.

articleTitle: Passive asymmetric propagation waveguide based on phase gradient metasurface
abstract: In this paper, we propose a design of asymmetric rectangular waveguide based on a phase gradient metasurface (PGMs). This metasurface consists of split-ring resonators with different geometric parameters, which can control the phase of the reflection wave and realize anomalous reflections. By loading the designed metasurface to a rectangular waveguide, propagation mode and direction of the guided waves can be controlled via strong anomalous reflection. Such waveguide device can converts the waveguide mode gradually into surface wave (SW) mode in forward direction, however, blocks it in backward direction. This design has been demonstrated by simulation results.

articleTitle: A novel broadband circularly polarized square ring microstrip antenna with four L-shaped strips shorted
abstract: A novel wideband circularly polarized (CP) Square Ring microstrip antenna with four shorted L-shaped strips is proposed. The antenna is fed by a compact broadband phase shifting network for circularly polarized. Four shorted L-shaped strips attached to the radiation patch and the coupling-feed are employed for wideband operation. From the simulated results, it is observed that the impedance bandwidth (S11<;-10dB) of the proposed antenna is 56.7% (1.15-2.06 GHz) and the 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of the proposed antenna is 69.7% (1.0-2.07 GHz).

articleTitle: Multi-channel filtering circuits based on dielectric resonators
abstract: Dielectric resonator (DRs) are widely used in based stations since they can offer high Q factor and feature high power handling. However, they often suffer from bulky size and heavy weight. Since a large amount of filtering circuit are needed in wireless systems, such as the 5G massive MIMO system, the size and weight reduction is of great importance. Aiming at this problem, two filtering circuits are designed by using the same sets of resonators and they can be integrated as one dual-channel circuit accordingly. The EM-filed properties of DR are studied for guiding the realization of isolation between two channels. By using this method, the number of DRs and cavities are reduced. Compared to the conventional two independent filtering circuits, the size of the presented dual-channel circuit can be reduced by more than 40% and thus, the weight and cost are also substantially reduced. This talk focuses on the design techniques for the DR-based dual-channel filtering circuits. The design examples with a variety of configurations will be presented.

articleTitle: Coupling matrix sign reversal transformation
abstract: This paper explores a new transformation of coupling matrix (CM) called sign reversal technique. It is mathematically proved that, sign reversal transformation holds S-parameter invariant property by preserving eigen values and eigen vectors of original CM. It is also showed that, sign reversal operation offer another type of similarity transformation. Proposed sign reversal technique is independent of filter order and coupling topology. Also, this technique is equally applicable to resonating as well as non-resonating nodes which provide more degree of freedom for design. Two different lossless filter examples are examined to verify this technique. Finally, a 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>-order inline bandpass filter is designed and simulated to illustrate sign reversal technique in bandpass frequency domain.

articleTitle: Broadband dielectric measurement using an open-ended coaxial based on time domain analysis with improved accuracy at low frequencies
abstract: An open-ended coaxial is commonly used in liquid complex permittivity measurements at microwave frequencies. In this paper, an improved method with simplified calibration is proposed. Time domain gating method is utilized to remove unwanted reflections. A mapping relation between complex permittivity and complex reflection coefficient is formed by full-wave simulation. A splicing method is applied. Measurements of distilled water, ethanol and methanol as well as their uncertainty analysis are carried out to verify the proposed method. The results agree well with reference data. The proposed method shows improved accuracy at low frequencies.

articleTitle: A miniaturized UHF dual-band circularly-polarized antenna
abstract: This paper presents a miniaturized UHF dual-band (345/390MHz) circularly-polarized (CP) four-element sequential rotation array antenna for airborne Satcom applications. Two planar Inverted-F antenna (PIFA) sub-elements, one as the driven sub-element and the other, in parallel with the driven one, as the parasitic sub-element, form each basic radiating element, based on which dual-band operation is realized. Four radiating elements are closely spaced and alternately overlapped in a sequential rotation manner, resulting in a compact structure (0.25×0.25λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). In this way, the antenna could make the most of the available space, and thus achieve good impedance bandwidth and gain performance. Besides, the sub-elements and elements configuration ensures similar current distributions and effective electrical apertures at two bands, which produces close gains and radiation patterns. A prototype is designed, fabricated and measured, and the results prove the good performance of proposed design.

articleTitle: Joint detection in uplink of massive MIMO system
abstract: In this article, the joint detection in uplink are studied in Massive MIMO (Massive Multiple-input Multiple-output) system. This article will combine interference estimation with soft detection, and finally propose a new structure for joint detection in uplink based on 5G simulation test platform of NCRL (National Mobile Communications Research Laboratory of SEU) and analysis feasibility of the new structure and give out simulation results.

articleTitle: The transmission characteristics study of multi attitude reception magnetic coupling resonance wireless energy transmission system
abstract: This paper used circuit theory and calculation of mutual inductance between transmitting and receiving coil to model and simulate the characteristic of the one and two dimension resonant wireless power transmission system. It studies the relationship between transmission characteristics and the coil parameters. The selection method of radius and turn number of one and two dimension coil is established. In the case of large angle rotation and horizontal migration of the receiving coil, it compares the receiving power of one and two dimension coil. Finally, it proves that the two dimensional multi attitude resonant coil designed in this paper can achieve full angle and high power energy transmission compared with the traditional one dimension coil through the experiment.

articleTitle: A high-precision sideband suppression model for transmitter leakage compensation
abstract: In this paper, a novel high-precision sideband suppression model is proposed for the compensation of transmitter leakage. By further exploiting the merits of dual-band modeling methodology and decomposed vector rotation behavioral model in sideband modeling, this proposed model can achieve significant suppression performance with relatively low computational complexity in model construction. The experimental results have shown a great validation that the unwanted distortion can be suppressed over 50 dB by employing this proposed model.

articleTitle: Reactive frequency downconverter for low power harvesting applications
abstract: This paper proposes a varactor-based or reactive device-based frequency downconverter for low power harvesting applications. Theoretical formulation is derived to estimate the conversion efficiency. For demonstration purpose, a frequency downconverter with output frequency of 800 MHz is developed using two input frequencies of 2.4 GHz and 1.6 GHz. Considering practical situations, the two input signals are set to have an equal power level. A reasonable agreement is obtained between the simulated and calculated results. It was found that the varactor can achieve a high conversion efficiency above 90% in the case of no harmonic and matching losses. The prototype was fabricated and measured. When the two input powers are around −20 dBm, the measured output power is around −37 dBm. This preliminary result can be improved using a more accurate varactor model in future measurements.

articleTitle: A novel real voltage offset controlled envelope shaping function for multilevel supply modulated power amplifier
abstract: In this paper, a novel envelope shaping function for multilevel (ML) supply modulated power amplifier (PA) is proposed to control the real voltage offset (RVO) between the ML discrete supply modulator and the PA. The RVO of some general shaping functions will be analyzed and compared. With a specified RVO, the proposed function is derived after getting the new thresholds of ML supply modulator. The linearity and efficiency of the ML supply modulated PA can be controlled by the proposed function. For a 10 MHz bandwidth OFDM signal with 8.5 dB peak-to-average ratio, the proposed method is applied to maximize the efficiency of the PA with a saturated power of 48 dBm. The efficiency of the PA at an average power of 39.5 dBm is 4.6% higher than no shaping of the envelope.

articleTitle: The Fano resonant model of two-arm resonator in waveguide
abstract: The RLC circuit model, named the Lorentz model, is commonly used for resonator. But when the resonators are strongly coupled with each other, the principle of superposition does not work. Traditional Lorentz model can not describe the interaction between wave modes, and Fano's resonance model is used. The paper introduces the background for the two resonant models. And then the behaviors of a two-arm resonant model in a waveguide are simulated and measured, the results of them are basically accordance.

articleTitle: Transparency effect based on hybridization interaction in individual metamaterial resonator
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate that the transparency effect based on the hybridization interaction can be achieved in individual three-gap split ring resonator (SRR). When the symmetry of the SRR metamaterial is broken, a pronounced transparency window appears in transmission spectrum. The resonance nature of the transparency effect is analyzed by employing the plasmonic hybridization. Numerical simulations also validate the strong dispersion property and the slow light property of the plasmonic metamaterial, which results in our plasmonic metamaterial that can be exploited to design terahertz slow light devices.

articleTitle: A 3.6 GHz BW, 8 GSamples/s, high IIP3 track-and-hold amplifier with Schottky diode and high linearity buffer in GaAs HBT technology
abstract: This paper presents a high-speed, low distortion track and hold amplifier (THA) in GaAs HBT. A series sample Schottky diode is added to switch emitter follower in order to improve the stability and speed of THA. Perturbation technique is used to analyze and discuss the nonlinearity distortion of input buffer, CAD results verifies the hand analysis. Experimental results show that the prototype THA achieves IIP3 more than +20dBm up to entire small-signal bandwidth of 3.6GHz with a sample rates of 8 Gs/s, and a SFDR of better than 38dB at 3GHz. In addition to HBT technology, DHBT and other technology can be used in this proposed THA.

articleTitle: A broadband SIW antenna array at ku band with a low mutual coupling
abstract: This work presents an antenna with low mutual coupling. A cavity backed SIW antenna is designed to work at Ku-band at first, the SIW antenna is radiated from the patch and slot, which is work from 12.11GHz to 15.16GHz. Then two elements are integrated to achieve an antenna array. In order to reduce the mutual coupling between the two SIW antennas, an metamaterial wall is inserted between two antennas, which is designed based on the periodic boundary conditions. The simulated scattering parameters show that a good isolation of -28.8 dB is achieved by using the metamaterial wall. And the proposed antenna performs well in radiation efficiency and gain from the simulated results.

articleTitle: An enhanced particle swarm optimization algorithm for deep space antenna array layout
abstract: Low sidelobe levels are necessary for deep space antenna array system. This paper presents an enhanced particle swarm optimization (EPSO) algorithm for a large antenna array whose elements spacing is much larger than the wavelength. The algorithm adds the optimal particle interference operator and a gradient operator. Adding those two operators can make the stagnant particles reactivate and prevent them from falling into the local optimal solution. The large antenna array consists of 34 elements which has a diameter of 12 m, located in an area of 500 m × 900 m. The simulation results show that the The maximum sidelobe level of the array pattern is -12.84 dB.

articleTitle: A frequency extension module for W-band antenna measurement facility
abstract: A frequency extension module for W-band antenna measurement facility is presented in this paper. The proposed frequency extension module includes a transmitting extender as well as a receiving extender. Active frequency multiplying and high order harmonic mixing are adopted in the two extenders, respectively. The developed extension module covers 92-96 GHz band and features characteristics of 15 dBm of output power and 113 dB of dynamic range. This set of extension module is fully compatible with commercial instruments and provides a cost-effective solution for W-band antenna measurement facilities.

articleTitle: Ultra-wide dynamic range rectifier topology for multi-sine wireless powered endoscopic capsules
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wide dynamic range rectifier topology is proposed in order to solve the rectifier's early-breakdown problem in the multi-sine wireless powered endoscopic capsule applications. This proposed rectifier topology realizes an extended reverse breakdown voltage while maintaining its forward turn-on voltage, which enables a high power conversion efficiency even with an ultra-high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) multi-sine excitation. Theoretical analysis and experiment results validate that the proposed circuit greatly increases its reverse breakdown voltage and maintains its forward turn-on voltage, which enables an ultra-wide dynamic power range for the multi-sine wireless powered endoscopic capsules.

articleTitle: A novel low-cost Ka-band transition from conventional waveguide to substrate integrated suspended waveguide
abstract: The substrate integrated suspended line (SISL) has high quality-factor and low substrate loss as the excited electronic and magnetic field mainly exists in the air cavity. To further reduce the dielectric loss especially for high frequency applications, a novel substrate integrated suspended waveguide (SISW) is proposed based on the SISL platform, and the transition from SISW to standard rectangle waveguide is also studied. The proposed SISW and transition only use low-cost FR4 and are fabricated by using standard printed circuit board (PCB) process. As a demonstration case, a Ka-band transition from WR-28 to SISW has been designed and fabricated. Dielectric excavation is also employed to further reduce the circuit loss. The implemented back-to-back transition shows a small insertion loss of only 0.31 dB, and the return loss is better than 21.2 dB from 26 GHz to 40GHz.

articleTitle: Microwave surface resistance/resistivity measurement using microstrip complementary split ring resonator sensor
abstract: This paper presents a complementary split ring resonator (CSRR) based sensor for non-contact microwave surface resistance/resistivity characterization of bulk conductors. Through full-wave simulations, we observed the dependence of |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub>| of CSRR on surface resistance/resistivity of bulk conductor which is placed on top of the CSRR. Results show that the resonant frequency of the CSRR decreases monotonously with increasing surface resistance/resistivity. Experiments were performed with a CSRR resonating at around 1.9 GHz. Artificially roughened Aluminum plates were used as proof-of-principle samples. Surface resistance/resistivity of these samples was also measured using traditional cylindrical cavity resonator. Preliminary results show that it is possible to characterize surface resistance/resistivity using CSRR. The proposed sensor has the following advantages: low cost, non-contact and high spatial resolution.

articleTitle: 9/15GHz dual-band GaN monolithic power amplifier
abstract: This paper presents design and measurements of a 9/15 GHz dual-band monolithic power amplifier implemented in Nanjing Electronic Devices Institute's (NEDI's) 0.25-μm GaN on SiC HEMT process. Two second harmonic control branches were adopted in the design of inter-stage matching net-work(ISMN) to increase the efficiency of power amplifier. Large signal measurements exhibit saturated output power of 42dBm and 41.8dBm, and power added efficiency(PAE) of 40% and 35% at 9GHz and 15GHz in pulsed mode, respectively.

articleTitle: Simulation and analysis of near-field distribution of unmanned checkout channel
abstract: The analysis of near-field distribution of unmanned checkout channel (UCC) plays a guiding role on the design of the channel and the antenna inside it. However, limited by computer resources, it is difficult for traditional algorithms to achieve accurate simulation of such large-scale targets. With the development of the multi-core technology and the cluster technology, the parallel higher-order method of moments (HO-MoM) can be utilized to solve this problem. In this paper, the correctness of the algorithm is verified by comparing the far-field patterns of an antenna array with that computed by the finite-element method (FEM), and then the near-field distribution of the whole UCC is simulated, and the result is in good agreement with the actual measurement. It demonstrates the efficiency and accuracy of HO-MoM, and shows its capability in solving practical engineering problems.

articleTitle: An 18-GHz-bandwidth master-slave sample-and-hold amplifier for high-speed communication in 0.13um SiGe BiCMOS
abstract: Design and analysis of a fully-differential master-slave sample-and-hold amplifier (SHA) is presented in this paper using 0.13um SiGe BiCMOS process. To achieve broad bandwidth, Cherry-Hooper topology is employed in the input buffer of SHA. With feedthrough-attenuation capacitors and clock-controlled auxiliary transistors in track-hold switch, signal feed-through and clock feedthrough are reduced. To shorten trackhold transition time, sinusoidal clock signal is converted to square wave in clock buffer. Input bandwidth of 18GHz, spurious free dynamic rang above 33dB are measured for 2 GSample/s and -5dBm single-ended input signal. The proposed SHA is suit for high-speed high-broadband analog-to-digital converter used in high-speed wireless communication.

articleTitle: Distributed band elimination filters for real-time spectrum analyzer
abstract: This paper discusses on distributed band elimination filters (D-BEFs) for real-time spectrum analyzer. The D-BEF is composed of single-sided or double-sided open stubs with different length and strong electric fields are induced at the edge of specific stubs corresponding to input frequencies. Basic ideas are introduced and experimental verification from DC to 6 GHz is carried out successfully.
